scoring.implementation_coverage: lower bound: requirements with status IMPLEMENTED or TESTED divided by total requirements; unreviewed requirements count as incomplete
scoring.verified_completion: lower bound: requirements with status TESTED divided by total requirements; unreviewed requirements count as unverified
scoring.assessment_coverage: requirements with a status other than UNREVIEWED divided by total requirements
scoring.complete_when: all requirements are TESTED with passing evidence

requirements.text: The implementation agent MUST follow this document as the source of truth.
limitations: Meta/process requirement: compliance is demonstrated by the wave execution record and ADR practice, not by an automated check.

requirements.text: When implementation details appear ambiguous, use the most conservative behavior that preserves correctness and document the choice in an Architecture Decision Record (ADR).
limitations: Every ambiguity listed in strategy §3.5.1 now has a dedicated ADR (0005-0011, plus 0003/0004 from Wave 0); ADR coverage is reviewed, not machine-enforced.

requirements.text: Do not silently invent a less conservative shortcut.
limitations: Conservative-default rule (strategy §6.1) governs ambiguity resolution and each recorded decision carries a regression test where behavior changed; the invariant itself is enforced by review, not automation.

requirements.text: The words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY are normative requirements.
limitations: Meta-requirement defining how the LLD is interpreted; no standalone code artifact. Applied throughout the strategy document and all 12 ADRs.

requirements.text: Build a complete working product, not a toy proof of concept.
implementation: The functional gap register of the completion strategy is closed: the adapter fixture corpus and the equivalent-outcome contract suite (WP-A), the graph strategy with the derived index and the traversal bounds (WP-E), the scheduled audit orchestration and the calibration metrics (WP-F), the validation program with the nightly native job and the performance measurements (WP-H) and the observability wiring with an OTLP exporter (WP-K).
The product remains a working end-to-end system: the CLI indexes, plans, executes and uploads, the server plans, audits and quarantines, and the adapters discover the units of seven build systems.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-14: the whole program is green on this host: every unit, contract, end-to-end, performance and historical-replay suite passes, and the database-backed suites pass against a real PostgreSQL.
limitations: The native build tools are not installed on this host, so the native fixture suite runs in the nightly job; the repository's own coverage of the native adapters is the fixture corpus and the contract suite.

requirements.text: All selected commands MUST be executed as argument arrays without shell interpolation by default.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestExecutionFallbackMustBeArgvAndShellsAreRejectedAcrossPlatforms, TestRunnerChildProcess, TestRunnerRejectsRelativeExecutableTraversal, TestGenericRejectsShellInjectionAndTraversal — all product commands are exec.CommandContext argv arrays with no shell interpolation.

requirements.text: Never concatenate untrusted repository data into a shell command.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: shells (sh/bash/dash/zsh/cmd/powershell/pwsh) rejected in full_suite_argv (validate.go:250,266) and generic units (generic.go:282) — TestExecutionFallbackMustBeArgvAndShellsAreRejectedAcrossPlatforms, TestGenericRejectsShellInjectionAndTraversal; repository-wide review found no shell-interpolation call site in product code.

requirements.text: An incomplete, unsupported, stale, or contradictory impact graph MUST reduce optimization, never reduce verification.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestCreatePlanEscalatesWhenHardPathChangesOrGraphIsDangling, TestCreatePlanEscalatesForStaleFingerprintAndUnavailableFallback, TestMandatoryUnrunnableEscalationDetailIsDeterministic — incomplete/stale/dangling evidence forces full verification (escalation), never a narrower selection.

requirements.text: The product MUST preserve configured mandatory checks and security/compliance gates.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestRepositoryConfigCannotRemoveOrganizationMandatoryChecks, TestMandatoryUnrunnableEscalationDetailIsDeterministic — mandatory checks survive config merge and unrunnable mandatory checks escalate to full verification.

requirements.text: A planner recommendation MUST NOT silently override them.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestRepositoryConfigCannotWeakenOrganizationOrEnableRiskBasedCI plus analysis mandatory-check escalation tests — the planner cannot drop or downgrade mandatory checks and security/compliance gates.

requirements.text: A successful selected-test run MUST NOT be represented as proof that unselected tests would pass.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestCreatePlanBuildsExplainableTargetedPass asserts the explanation contains 'TARGETED_PASS' and 'nothing about unselected tests' (planner_test.go:28).

requirements.text: Every plan MUST be explainable: it must state what was selected, why it was selected, what was omitted, confidence limitations, and whether a safety fallback was applied.
implementation: internal/analysis/planner.go stage9Context renders the change summary (with the global-impact classification of every changed file), the snapshot identifiers, the adapter capability versions and the toolchain digest into every plan, and the escalation path preserves the omitted units as an audit trail (internal/analysis/planner.go fullRequired/omissionContext).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-14: TestStage9ExplanationCarriesChangeSummaryAndSnapshotIDs asserts that the ready plan, an escalated plan and a full-mode plan all carry the change summary, the snapshot identifiers, the adapter versions and the toolchain digest, and that an escalated plan records the omitted unit with the reason 'escalated to full verification'.
limitations: The explanation states the estimate and the evidence granularity; it never claims that a selective plan proves correctness.

requirements.text: Results MUST be measured at the level of accepted changes and complete validation outcomes, not merely number of tests selected or tokens consumed.
implementation: The accepted-change outcomes are recorded through the accepted-changes API (internal/service/backend.go) and the quality dashboards are computed from the persisted evidence: internal/audit/metrics.go computes the six LLD 10.6 calibration metrics with their breakdowns and internal/persistence/reads.go serves the calibrated metrics.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-14: the calibration metrics are asserted with their denominators and sample sizes (internal/audit/metrics_test.go) and the accepted-change outcome recording is asserted by the service and persistence suites.
limitations: A metric whose evidence is missing is reported as undefined with a reason, never as a measured zero.

requirements.text: Source files and full source contents MUST NOT be uploaded to the IVP API.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestSnapshotRejectsSourceContentMetadata, TestResultSummaryRejectsFreeFormText, TestPlanRequestRejectsUnsafeChangedPathAndUnknownField, TestReportSanitizerRemovesSourcePathsFreeformFailureTextAndSecrets — source files are never part of any accepted API payload.

requirements.text: The local executor may read source files; the server receives graph metadata, normalized paths, hashes, summaries, plans, and sanitized execution metadata only.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: snapshot/plan/result payload tests above plus artifact sanitizer tests (TestArtifactManagerSanitizesAndScopesUploadAndRetrieval) — server receives metadata, hashes, summaries and sanitized results only.

requirements.text: The application MUST work in an offline/degraded state by falling back to the locally configured full verification command when the server is unavailable or the policy/snapshot cannot be trusted.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestOfflinePolicyRequiresTrustedUnexpiredCompatibleSnapshot, TestCreatePlanEscalatesForStaleFingerprintAndUnavailableFallback, TestIncompleteIndexRequiresFullVerification (fresh run, 1.250s) — offline/degraded mode runs the local full-suite argv (runOfflineFullSuite, internal/cli/run.go:316; ADR 0006).

requirements.text: Do not add LLM inference to the safety-critical test-selection path.
limitations: Negative requirement verified by review 2026-11-03: no LLM/inference dependency exists in go.mod and no model call exists in the selection path; not machine-enforced as an invariant.

requirements.text: The initial mature system uses deterministic, observable decision logic.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestCreatePlanOrderingAndReasonsAreDeterministic (20 identical runs), TestGreedySetCoverUsesStableTieBreak, TestEvidenceReferencesStableOrderForEqualKeys — deterministic, observable scoring with stable tie-breaks.

requirements.text: Optional model-generated explanations are outside the core design and MUST NOT change selected checks.
limitations: No model integration exists anywhere in the repository (no ML/LLM dependencies in go.mod); explanations are template-built from deterministic planner state. Negative requirement, not machine-enforced.

requirements.text: Do not introduce placeholder implementations, unimplemented adapter stubs, TODO-only acceptance criteria, or “future phase” sections.
limitations: Review found no stub or TODO-only acceptance paths (strategy §1.1); tracked honesty gap: jest advertises ResultFormats junit-xml but Materialize never emits it (strategy §3.1.6).

requirements.text: For every supported adapter and API in this document, implement and test the behavior.
implementation: All seven adapters are implemented and tested against the checked-in fixture corpus (126 fixtures: eleven categories per adapter across two tool versions) with one shared equivalent-outcome contract test, and every API operation is implemented with its own assertions (internal/api).
The native execution path is exercised by the nightly job over the checked-in sample projects (tests/native/native_test.go).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-14: the adapter contract suite classifies every fixture of every adapter through one canonical classifier and asserts the identical outcome per category, and the API suite covers every registered operation including the cross-tenant artifact paths.
limitations: The native tool executions run in the nightly job; the fixture corpus and the contract suite cover the behaviour on this host.

requirements.text: Unsupported ecosystems MUST be handled through the generic adapter or conservative full-suite fallback.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestGenericDiscoversCheckKind, TestGenericRejectsUnknownTargetsAndDependencyCycles, TestAllBuiltinsExposeContractAndCapabilities, TestIncompleteIndexRequiresFullVerification — unsupported ecosystems use declared generic units or the conservative full-suite fallback (ADR 0009).

requirements.text: Pin production dependencies and container images to reproducible versions/digests in the implementation repository.
limitations: Pins verified by review 2026-11-03: go.mod exact versions, builder image golang:1.27.3-alpine3.24@sha256:d530cf60..., GitHub actions pinned to commit SHAs, GOTOOLCHAIN=local in CI; no automated pin-drift check yet (strategy §17.9).

requirements.text: Keep a software bill of materials and vulnerability scanning in CI.
limitations: govulncheck, Syft SBOM and Trivy image scans are wired in CI (ci.yml:104-109, release.yml:75-83) but execute only on GitHub Actions — not runnable on this host (strategy §17.9 release gates).

requirements.text: Coding agents and developers frequently run broad validation after a small edit, wait for slow build/test pipelines, and re-run checks whose results may no longer be informative.
limitations: Problem-statement row: addressed by the ivp plan/verify workflow that produces a scoped selective plan instead of a full re-run; the pain point itself has no direct test.

requirements.text: Conversely, naive change-based test selection can miss indirect dependencies and allow regressions to escape.
limitations: Indirect-dependency protection is implemented via graph traversal plus hard escalation (strategy §3.2 notes missing hard rules 3/4 remain open); end-to-end proof that indirect dependents are selected belongs to the §17.3 native-integration suite (Wave 3).

requirements.text: The complete implementation MUST support these explicit integration families:
implementation: All seven integration families of LLD 1.4 are implemented and directly asserted: Gradle (internal/adapters/gradle), Maven (internal/adapters/maven), Bazel (internal/adapters/bazel), pytest (internal/adapters/pytest), Jest (internal/adapters/jest), Nx (internal/adapters/nx) and the generic adapter (internal/adapters/generic), each with its own discovery, materialization and result-parsing assertions.

The per-family gaps of strategy 3.1.3-3.1.7 are closed: Gradle's '--tests' gate now requires Gradle's Test-task naming convention and runs unknown-type tasks whole (ADR 0008 as amended), Maven enforces surefire_enabled/failsafe_enabled as tri-state provider toggles (ADR 0007 as amended), Bazel resolves the configured target set and dependency graph with 'bazel cquery' and classifies skipped/timeout/flaky BEP outcomes while merging every report file, Jest emits the JUnit report it advertises and resolves multi-project configurations, and pytest ingests coverage.py per-test contexts (LLD 8.6).

Strategy 3.1.9 (config validation depth) is closed in internal/adapters/native/base.go:28-100: native adapters validate the configured report paths, coverage paths and the full-suite argv instead of only NUL bytes.

The SCIP enrichment input (LLD 1.4, optional) is resolved by ADR 0016: no symbol index is consumed, the file/build-target granularity is the operating mode, and the symbol consumer path is implemented and asserted.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: the family rows of LLD 1.4 are each directly asserted and green - Gradle (TestSupportsGradleTestFilterAcceptsOnlyTestTasks, TestGradleMaterializeAppliesTestFilterOnlyToSupportedTasks, TestGradleMaterializeRunsWholeTaskWhenTaskTypeIsUnknown, TestGradleDiscoveryDeclaresClassLevelOnlyCapability), Maven (TestMavenDiscoveryOmitsSurefireUnitsWhenDisabled, TestMavenDiscoveryOmitsFailsafeUnitsWhenDisabled, TestMavenDiscoveryKeepsUnitsWhenProviderKeysUnset, TestMavenDiscoveryKeepsVerifyUnitOnlyWithVisibleFailsafe, TestMavenMaterializeRefusesDisabledProviderGoals), Bazel (TestBazelCQueryFailureKeepsQueryDerivedEvidence, TestBazelCQueryConfiguredOnlyTargetIsDiscovered, TestBazelDiscoveryIsDeterministicAndNeverRunsTests, TestParseBEPClassifiesSkippedTimeoutAndFlakyOutcomes, TestParseResultsMergesEveryDeclaredReportFile), Jest (TestMaterializeDeclaresJUnitReportAndReporter, TestJunitReporterWritesJunitXML, TestJestProjectResolutionPicksOwningProject, TestJestMultiProjectDiscoveryAttributesTargetsToProjects), pytest (TestCoveragePyPerTestContextsAreParsed, TestPerTestCoverageObservationsAreAttributedToTheirTest) and the shared parser/config validation (TestValidateConfigRejectsUnsafePathsAndArgv, internal/adapters/native/base_test.go:13).

PASS on 2026-11-12: go test ./internal/adapters/... -count=1 is green for all seven families (gradle, maven, bazel, pytest, jest, nx, generic) and go test ./... -count=1 is green across all packages; the cross-adapter equivalent-outcome contract test (internal/adapters/equivalent_outcome_test.go) still passes with the 126-fixture corpus.
limitations: No native build tool (gradle, maven, bazel, nx, jest, pytest) exists on this host, so every family's command construction and result parsing is asserted over fixtures and the injected capture seam; real tool execution stays CI-only (nightly native integration).
The optional SCIP/symbol-index input is deliberately not consumed (ADR 0016): the consumer path is asserted but no producer exists, so file and build-target granularity remain the operating mode.

The umbrella row asserts the completeness of the family coverage; each family's own limitations (effective-POM inheritance, task typing, configured-query scope, project-configuration resolution) are recorded on its own row.

requirements.text: Family | Supported target behavior | Evidence and execution mechanism
limitations: Table-header row: its content is the column structure of the §1.4 integration-family table; the actual requirements are the per-family rows IVP-1-4-dab5c9f276 through IVP-1-4-2d89b4d7d9, reviewed individually.

requirements.text: Gradle | Multi-project JVM builds; task graph; test task discovery; class/method-filtered unit tests; configured integration-test tasks | Gradle wrapper/CLI, project/task metadata, test reports, JaCoCo XML when configured
implementation: internal/adapters/gradle/gradle.go:329-334 supportsGradleTestFilter now recognizes Gradle's Test-task naming convention only (the task named 'test' or a name ending in the camel-case suffix 'Test', e.g. integrationTest/unitTest), so a task whose type is unknown runs the whole task (LLD 8.2 line 590); no task typing is executed and the discovery candidate rule is unchanged (ADR 0008, amended 2026-11-12).

internal/adapters/gradle/gradle.go:298-303 the gate call site and the '--tests' append (class-level filters only, derived from changed sources at gradle.go:344-382); gradle.go:26 advertises SelectableGranularity GRADLE_TASK, CoveragePrecision CLASS_OR_FILE and SupportsFiltering true, with no method-level claim; gradle.go:177 declares each candidate with GRADLE_TASK granularity and Filterable true.

internal/adapters/gradle/gradle_test.go:40-254 four new table-driven tests pin the honest-capability contract (gate table, materialize positive/negative, whole-task fallback for unknown types, discovery capability declarations).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestSupportsGradleTestFilterAcceptsOnlyTestTasks, TestGradleMaterializeAppliesTestFilterOnlyToSupportedTasks, TestGradleMaterializeRunsWholeTaskWhenTaskTypeIsUnknown and TestGradleDiscoveryDeclaresClassLevelOnlyCapability (internal/adapters/gradle/gradle_test.go:40-254) - the '--tests' gate accepts only 'test'/'integrationTest'/'unitTest' and rejects 'compileTestJava', 'compileTestKotlin', 'testClasses', the empty name and 'latest'; Materialize emits no '--tests' and sets Filtered=false for a gate-rejected task (args exactly [:app:compileTestJava, --console=plain]) while a gate-accepted task is narrowed to exactly [:app:test, --console=plain, --tests, com.example.app.AppTest] with Filtered=true; discovered candidates keep SelectableGranularity GRADLE_TASK, Filterable true and no method-level claim.

PASS on 2026-11-12: the discovery candidate rule is unchanged and asserted - compileTestJava is still a discoverable candidate (internal/adapters/gradle/gradle_test.go:32) and remains neutralized only by the execution-time ZERO_TESTS/REPORT_PARSE infra-failure guard, never by a pass.
limitations: The gate is a naming convention, not task typing (ADR 0008): no 'gradle help --task' or configuration-phase introspection runs. A real Test task with a non-conventional name (allTests, lowercase unittest) is not narrowed and runs whole - conservative over-verification, never under-verification.

The discovery candidate rule stays a name heuristic, so compileTestJava-style false positives remain discoverable units; the DiscoveryReliable:true / confidence 0.60 tension remains an open gap (strategy 3.1.3).
Filtering is class-level only: no method-level selector is emitted or claimed (GRADLE_TASK is the only granularity claimed).
No Gradle binary exists on this host, so command construction is asserted over the fixture capture seam; real Gradle execution stays CI-only.

requirements.text: Maven | Reactor modules; Surefire and Failsafe test goals; class/method filtering where provider supports it | Maven wrapper/CLI, effective reactor/project metadata, XML test reports, JaCoCo XML when configured
implementation: internal/adapters/maven/maven.go:109-129 the surefire_enabled / failsafe_enabled keys are read at discovery and their effect is reported ('Surefire disabled by configuration; no surefire test units declared' / 'Failsafe disabled by configuration; no failsafe verify units declared'); maven.go:181-188 declares '<module>#test' only when Surefire is enabled and '<module>#verify' only when Failsafe is enabled AND the module's own build/pluginManagement shows maven-failsafe-plugin; maven.go:272-277 refuses to materialize a goal of a disabled provider.

Tri-state plumbing so an absent key can never mean disabled: internal/config/types.go:149-159 (MavenConfig.SurefireEnabled/FailsafeEnabled are *bool with omitempty), internal/config/defaults.go:41 (both default to true), internal/config/adapter.go:26-31 (config -> adapter view mapping), internal/adapters/adapter.go:126-138 (AdapterConfig tri-state fields plus the exported ProviderEnabled helper, nil means unset).
internal/adapters/maven/maven_provider_test.go (new) and internal/config/config_test.go:449-491 assert the disabled/unset/enabled behavior and the plumbing.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestMavenDiscoveryOmitsSurefireUnitsWhenDisabled, TestMavenDiscoveryOmitsFailsafeUnitsWhenDisabled, TestMavenDiscoveryKeepsUnitsWhenProviderKeysUnset, TestMavenDiscoveryKeepsVerifyUnitOnlyWithVisibleFailsafe and TestMavenMaterializeRefusesDisabledProviderGoals (internal/adapters/maven/maven_provider_test.go:51-184) - with surefire_enabled false no '#test' unit is declared and the Surefire reason is reported, with failsafe_enabled false no '#verify' unit is declared and the Failsafe reason is reported, unset keys keep the ADR 0007 unit set {#test, #verify, service#test} with no provider reason, an enabled Failsafe without a visible maven-failsafe-plugin still declares no '#verify' unit, and materializing a disabled provider's goal fails.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestMavenProviderTogglesReachAdapterConfig (internal/config/config_test.go:454) asserts the tri-state mapping end to end - defaults map to enabled, an explicit 'surefire_enabled: false' reaches the adapter view as false, an omitted key stays enabled, and a config without the keys keeps both toggles unset (nil).
limitations: Enforcement is adapter-wide, not per module; there is no per-module provider override.

surefire_enabled true still does not prove a Surefire provider exists (no effective-POM/parent inheritance, ADR 0007 unchanged), so such a unit may still report zero tests and be classified ZERO_TESTS.
failsafe_enabled true still requires maven-failsafe-plugin to be visible in the module's own build/pluginManagement.

Disabling a provider removes those units from the snapshot inventory, so such repositories follow the existing 'no tests selected -> FULL_SUITE' policy; no new escalation path was added and DiscoveryResult.Complete semantics are unchanged.

The published JSON Schema still types both keys as plain booleans - unsetness exists only as a Go-side concept (the fields carry omitempty so an unset key is omitted rather than serialized as null); Config.Adapters.Maven.SurefireEnabled/FailsafeEnabled are now *bool and every future consumer must treat nil as 'unset -> provider enabled'.

requirements.text: Bazel | Test targets and configured dependency graph | bazel query/cquery/test listing and bazel test; coverage/report formats supported by the repository setup
implementation: internal/adapters/bazel/bazel.go:95-273 discovery resolves the configured test-target set with 'bazel cquery' and the configured dependency graph with 'bazel cquery --output=graph', while keeping the unconfigured 'bazel query' graph; bazel.go:59-93 declares the evidence sources and confidences (bazel:query-graph 0.80, bazel:cquery-graph 0.85, bazel:cquery-target-set 0.60, bazel:target-package-membership 0.50).

internal/adapters/bazel/bazel.go:446-461 ParseResults now parses every declared report file (parseBEPSet) instead of only the first, and bazel.go:467-773 classifies passed/failed/skipped/timeout/flaky in the existing adapters outcome vocabulary (timeout maps to 'error' because the shared vocabulary has no timeout constant, flaky is expressed by keeping every attempt of a target under the same name).

internal/adapters/bazel/bazel_cquery_test.go (new), internal/adapters/bazel/bazel_bep_test.go (new) and internal/adapters/bazel/bazel_fixture_test.go:106-249 assert the configured-query behavior, the BEP categories and the multi-report merge.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestBazelCQueryFailureKeepsQueryDerivedEvidence, TestBazelCQueryConfiguredOnlyTargetIsDiscovered, TestBazelDiscoveryIsDeterministicAndNeverRunsTests and TestBazelFixtureDetectDiscoverMaterialize (internal/adapters/bazel/bazel_cquery_test.go:50-210, bazel_fixture_test.go:106-249) - the adapter resolves the configured test-target set with 'bazel cquery kind(".*_test rule", deps(//...)) --output=label' and the configured graph with 'bazel cquery deps(set(...)) --output=graph', keeps the unconfigured query graph, records a DiscoveryResult reason and no configured evidence when cquery fails, and never executes a test during discovery.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestParseBEPClassifiesSkippedTimeoutAndFlakyOutcomes, TestParseBEPTimeoutFlagIsClassifiedAsError, TestParseResultsMergesEveryDeclaredReportFile, TestParseResultsConsumesEveryGlobMatchedReportFile and TestParseResultsReadsTheMaterializedReportFile (internal/adapters/bazel/bazel_bep_test.go:38-176) - the BEP parser classifies passed/failed/skipped/timeout/flaky and merges every declared report file deterministically, sorted by test id and independent of the declared path order.
limitations: No bazel binary exists on this host, so the command shapes and the parse paths are asserted only through the adapter's injectable capture seam and inline BEP fixtures; real 'bazel cquery'/'bazel test' execution stays CI-only.

The shared adapters outcome vocabulary has no timeout or flaky constant: timeout maps to the closest existing category ('error') and flaky is expressed by keeping every attempt of the target under the same test name, so the existing duplicate-case detection classifies it; no shared constant was added.

BuildTarget carries label-level provenance only, so the recorded dependencies are the conservative union of the unconfigured and configured graphs and per-edge provenance is not representable in the shared shape.

The affected-target computation still uses the unconfigured 'bazel query ... rdeps(...)' because cquery cannot traverse source-file targets; only target selection and the dependency graph use the configured query.

requirements.text: Nx | Project graph and affected project targets; Jest target execution and configured other Nx test targets | Nx CLI project/target graph, affected calculation, target-specific execution
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-03: TestNxProjectListFixturesAreSortedAndDeduplicated, TestNxProjectTargetFixtureIncludesJestConfigurationAndReportOptions, TestNxProjectListRejectsMalformedFixture, TestSupportedAdaptersMaterializeOnlySnapshotKnownTargets — project/target graph via nx show projects, native affected calculation (nx.go:207), jest and configured target execution.

requirements.text: pytest | Test file/node selection, JUnit XML result parsing, coverage mapping | pytest collection, node IDs, JUnit XML, coverage.py XML and per-test contexts when configured
implementation: internal/adapters/reports.go:551,565,600-614 the coverage.py JSON parser now reads the report's per-file 'contexts' map (line number -> test contexts) and exposes them as per-test coverage: adapters.CoverageResult.Contexts (internal/adapters/adapter.go:229-247) maps a context name to the files and line numbers that test executed.

internal/adapters/reports.go:412-450 ParseCoverageReports merges the per-test contexts across reports (deduplicating and sorting the line numbers) and normalizeCoveragePaths (reports.go:473-500) normalizes the context file paths exactly like the suite-level file paths, so a context can never point outside the repository.

internal/cli/run.go:1251-1314 collectCoverageObservations emits per-test coverage when the report carries contexts: every context is resolved to a discovered test unit (the pytest-cov '<node id>|<phase>' suffix is stripped by contextUnitKey, run.go:1316), every covered line becomes a test-specific, line-precision observation (Precision=LINE, SuiteLevel=false, TestSpecific=true, confidence 0.95), and a context that matches no discovered unit is ignored and reported instead of being attributed.

internal/persistence/plans_executions.go:402-407 the guard that forced every submitted coverage observation to be suite-level now enforces the same rule as the snapshot ingestion path (repositories.go:302-307): an observation is either test-specific or suite-level, never both and never neither.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestCoveragePyPerTestContextsAreParsed (internal/adapters/reports_test.go:77) asserts that a coverage.py JSON report with per-file contexts yields the context 'tests/test_api.py::test_add|run' covering lines 1 and 2 of pkg/test_api.py and the context 'tests/test_api.py::test_sub|run' covering line 2 only, while the suite-level result (3 statements, 2 covered) stays exactly as before - and that a report without contexts carries no context at all.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestPerTestCoverageObservationsAreAttributedToTheirTest and TestPerTestCoverageObservationsAreAbsentWithoutContexts (internal/cli/coverage_contexts_test.go:15,85) assert that a context is attributed to the discovered unit it names (phase suffix stripped), that every attributed observation is line-precision and test-specific with the right covered source, that a context matching no discovered unit is ignored and reported rather than attributed, and that a report without contexts produces no per-test evidence at all.
limitations: Per-test contexts are read from the coverage.py JSON report, which is where coverage.py writes them; the Cobertura XML writer does not emit a contexts element, so a XML-only report keeps the suite-level behaviour.

The pytest adapter's declared coverage precision stays FILE because per-test contexts are optional ('when configured'); a report that carries contexts is ingested as line-precision, test-specific evidence.

Context attribution requires the context name to match a discovered unit key exactly (after the phase suffix is stripped); a renamed or parametrized node id that does not match is ignored and reported, never attributed to a different test.

No pytest or coverage.py binary exists on this host, so the parsing and the attribution are asserted over fixtures; a real pytest --cov-context run stays CI-only, and the persistence-side acceptance of test-specific observations is exercised by the PostgreSQL-backed integration tests.

requirements.text: Core code impact inputs may additionally consume SCIP-compatible symbol/reference indexes.

The consumer path is implemented, not stubbed: internal/analysis/planner.go:1497-1508 precisionForNode maps a NodeSymbol to SYMBOL coverage precision and planner.go:1590-1599 reasonForPrecision emits COVERS_CHANGED_SYMBOL, so symbol evidence maps correctly whenever a producer arrives; internal/analysis/planner.go:1442-1478 maps observations onto impacted entities at file granularity and gates line precision on diff hunks.
internal/analysis/planner_completeness_test.go:671-691 asserts the disposition directly: impact analysis never invents a symbol-level entity and stays at file granularity without a symbol index.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestSCIPEnrichmentIsAbsentByDecisionAndKeepsImpactAtFileGranularity (internal/analysis/planner_completeness_test.go:671) asserts that impact analysis over a file-level graph yields exactly one impacted entity keyed 'file:src/main.go' with path 'src/main.go' and never a symbol-level entity, so the optional SCIP input is absent by decision rather than by accident.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestChangedLinesMapAtFileGranularityWithoutSymbolIndex (internal/analysis/planner_completeness_test.go:479) asserts the operating mode in both directions - line-precision coverage outside the diff hunks never maps to COVERS_CHANGED_LINE, and a symbol-precision observation maps to COVERS_CHANGED_SYMBOL while no symbol reason is fabricated when no symbol evidence exists.
limitations: The optional SCIP enrichment is deliberately not consumed (ADR 0016); the repository contains no SCIP/scc integration and no symbol-index producer, so the consumer path is asserted directly but never exercised end-to-end by a producer.
Adding a producer later needs no schema or algorithm-version change, because NodeSymbol and COVERS_CHANGED_SYMBOL are already in the domain vocabulary.

requirements.text: Graph storage: relational tables in PostgreSQL with indexed edge traversal and adjacency materialized views/cache as necessary; no separate graph database.
implementation: Graph storage stays relational in PostgreSQL with no separate graph database: the raw graph (graph_nodes, graph_edges) is the source of truth, the edge tables are indexed for traversal, and row-level security and append-only triggers are already installed by the migrations (internal/persistence/migrations/001_init.sql).

internal/analysis/derived_index.go:29-66,161-215 the adjacency materialized views/cache that the row allows 'as necessary' are now provided as a read-only derived index: adjacency lists by edge type, connected target/module mappings and the affected-target index are derived once per snapshot and cached by snapshot hash and algorithm version (ADR 0021).
internal/analysis/planner.go:247-257 the planner reads the cached index instead of issuing recursive traversal work per request, so a plan never walks the unbounded repository graph directly.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: the derived index that plays the role of the adjacency cache is directly asserted - TestDerivedIndexCarriesAdjacencyAndAffectedTargets and TestDerivedIndexIsCachedBySnapshotHashAndAlgorithmVersion (internal/analysis/derived_index_test.go:12,70) - and the persistence suite (internal/persistence) is green, so the relational storage, the migrations and the append-only triggers are unchanged.
PASS on 2026-11-12: go test ./... -count=1 is green across all packages, so the relational graph storage and the new derived index coexist without changing any stored graph.
limitations: The adjacency cache is an in-process derived index rather than a SQL materialized view: the stored graph and its indexes are unchanged, so a database-side query still uses the existing edge indexes (ADR 0021 decision 1).
The derived index is not shared between processes (CLI and server each keep their own), and it is rebuilt after a restart.
The executions index on (repository, status, started_at) required by LLD line 880 is still missing from the schema; it belongs to row IVP-13-2-28f4c3948f and remains open.

requirements.text: Binary files cannot use line-level coverage and therefore lower selection confidence unless build metadata identifies their consumers.
implementation: internal/gitutil/git.go:91-99,229-268,284-296 the Git producer marks a change binary from Git's own 'Binary files ... differ' diff marker (authoritative for tracked modifications, deletions and renames) and from a NUL-byte scan of the working-tree file (covering added and untracked files that are not part of the diff), populating the existing domain.ChangedFile.IsBinary field.

internal/analysis/planner.go:640,660-668 a coverage observation whose covered path is binary is never used at line granularity: its precision is downgraded to file granularity before the quality factor and the reason code are computed, so no COVERS_CHANGED_LINE claim is made for binary content.

internal/analysis/planner.go:418,1020,1029-1075 selection confidence is multiplied by the documented factor binaryConfidenceFactor (0.75) when a binary change's consumers are NOT identified by build metadata, and the existing LOW_SELECTION_CONFIDENCE rule then decides the outcome; the escalation detail names the affected binary paths. ADR 0020 (docs/adr/0020-binary-changes-lower-selection-confidence.md) records the decision and its alternatives.
internal/gitutil/git_test.go:136-166 and internal/analysis/planner_completeness_test.go:693-752 assert both sides of the rule.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestDetectChangesMarksBinaryFiles (internal/gitutil/git_test.go:136) asserts that a modified binary asset in the same change set as a modified text file is marked IsBinary while the text file is not.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestBinaryChangeLowersSelectionConfidenceWithoutIdentifiedConsumers (internal/analysis/planner_completeness_test.go:693) - a binary change whose consumers are unknown lowers selection confidence, escalates with LOW_SELECTION_CONFIDENCE and names the binary path ('binary change without build-metadata consumers lowers confidence: src/main.go'), while the same binary change with a DEPENDS_ON edge that identifies the consumer keeps the confidence, stays READY and produces no COVERS_CHANGED_LINE reason.
limitations: The confidence factor (0.75) is a documented judgment call, not an LLD-specified value (ADR 0020); an unset binary change therefore falls below the normal policy threshold and escalates, which is the conservative direction.

'Build metadata identifies their consumers' is implemented as the dependency graph naming them (a binary node with known reverse-dependency consumers); a binary file that is not in the graph is therefore penalized.

Binary detection depends on Git's diff marker and a NUL-byte scan of the working tree; a deleted binary file is detected by the diff marker only, and a binary file with no diff representation at all is not detected.

requirements.text: integration/E2E tests;
implementation: internal/analysis/planner.go:1005-1025 planExecutionTier tier 4 = candidate carrying ReasonIntegrationBoundary, ordered after high-risk consumers and before remaining tests (ADR 0017).

requirements.text: Available only when enabled by organization policy after calibration requirements have been met.

requirements.text: Runs selected suites for eligible low/medium-risk changes, but never omits mandatory checks.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestMandatoryUnrunnableEscalationDetailIsDeterministic (planner_test.go:110-149) asserts mandatory checks are always represented and never silently dropped, and TestValidatePlanRechecksWorktreePolicyTargetsAndMandatoryChecks (runner_test.go:94-110) asserts mandatory checks are revalidated before execution - a selection cannot omit them.

requirements.text: Full suite is required for high/unknown risk and hard-trigger changes.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: the hard-path subtest (planner_test.go:64-73) asserts a hard-trigger change forces FULL_REQUIRED with EscConfigOrToolchainChange, and the stale/unavailable-policy subtest (planner_test.go:41-61) asserts the same for unsafe state.

requirements.text: Runs shadow/audit full-suite executions at the configured sampling rate, plus scheduled full-suite audits.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-01: TestAuditSampleRateIsScopedToPlanMode asserts modes.risk_based_ci.audit_sample_rate governs RISK_BASED_CI plans and safety.audit.sample_rate every other mode, with the rate source named; TestAuditSampleSelectedIsDeterministicAndBounded asserts the sampling decision is a deterministic function of the execution id with rates 0 and 1 as hard bounds.

requirements.text: Automatically quarantines the affected selection scope on a confirmed or unresolved miss.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: classifier_test.go:30-39 asserts a confirmed omitted failure quarantines (DispositionConfirmed, Quarantine=true, CONFIRMED_MISS) and classifier_test.go:52-60 asserts an unresolved/ambiguous miss quarantines (DispositionPossible, Quarantine=true).
limitations: The RISK_BASED_CI mode context is never driven by a test (disabled by default, config_test.go:19-21), and writing the QUARANTINED row and forcing full verification for the scope (audits.go:95-98, planner.go:174-177) run only in the PostgreSQL path - CI-only.

requirements.text: selection_confidence is computed from: graph completeness, edge confidence, evidence freshness, adapter granularity/precision, mapped-weight coverage, historical sample size, toolchain comparability, and whether critical entities have test mappings.
limitations: calculateConfidence implements all eight listed inputs as a fixed weighted sum - graph completeness (:773-776), edge confidence (:777), evidence freshness (:778-781), adapter granularity/precision (:782-802), mapped-weight coverage (mapped parameter, clamped at :836), historical sample size (:803-814), toolchain/environment comparability (:815-818) and critical-entity test mapping (:819-835), with weights 0.20/0.15/0.15/0.10/0.20/0.05/0.10/0.05 at :836 - but no test asserts the composition, the weights, or any individual feature's contribution (planner_test.go:25 asserts only that the result clears the 0.98 gate).

requirements.text: It is not model confidence and must not be trained from unverified task-success labels.
limitations: Selection confidence is a deterministic weighted sum over evidence features with hard-coded weights (planner.go:772-838); no training, fitting, or task-success-label path exists anywhere in internal/analysis (verified by search), satisfying 'not model confidence' by construction - but no test asserts determinism or the absence of learned parameters.

requirements.text: Default minimum selection confidence: 0.98.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: config_test.go:16 asserts MinimumSelectionConfidence defaults to 0.98, and planner_test.go:25 asserts a READY plan's SelectionConfidence >= 0.98 (below-threshold plans fail the gate at planner.go:362-365).

requirements.text: If a required feature is missing, return UNKNOWN instead of substituting a favorable default.
limitations: No UNKNOWN sentinel exists: selection confidence is a float with no unknown state (VerificationPlan.SelectionConfidence), so a missing feature cannot be reported as UNKNOWN. Conservative substitutes are used instead: missing evidence lowers the computed confidence (zeros and penalties at planner.go:773-808 - never a favorable default), and unknown-evidence action is locked to FULL_SUITE (validate.go:83, defaults.go:21). The deviation from the LLD's UNKNOWN requirement is documented here; no test asserts the degradation path.

requirements.text: Before enabling RISK_BASED_CI, require the configured minimum number of observe-mode runs and audits, plus organization-owner approval.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-01: TestCalibrationCountsScopedToObserveModeExecutions counts only completed OBSERVE-mode executions with usable timing (varying mode, completion, outcome, and estimate one at a time) and only comparable audits.
PASS on 2026-10-30: TestRiskBasedCINeedsExplicitApprovalAndCompletedCalibration rejects RISK_BASED_CI without organization-owner approval and completed calibration.
limitations: Requires PostgreSQL; executes in the CI integration job (no Docker/PostgreSQL on the Windows development host).

requirements.text: The shipped default is disabled.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: config_test.go:19-21 (TestDefaultsImplementSafePlannerAndExecutionPolicy) asserts Modes.RiskBasedCI.EnabledByOrganizationPolicy is false in config.Defaults() - 'risk-based CI must be disabled by default'.

requirements.text: A confirmed miss or an audit that cannot be resolved immediately quarantines the affected repository/adapter/risk scope and forces full verification for that scope.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: classifier_test.go:30-39 asserts a confirmed miss quarantines and classifier_test.go:52-60 asserts an unresolvable (ambiguous/flaky) audit quarantines until human resolution - the quarantine decision for the affected scope.
limitations: Forcing full verification for that scope depends on policy.Quarantined reaching the planner (planner.go:174-177 EscQuarantineActive) and on server-side gating, asserted only by integration-tagged tests (internal/service/quarantine_gating_integration_test.go:52, requires PostgreSQL - CI-only); no local test sets policy.Quarantined.

requirements.text: Quarantine expires only after the configured period AND a maintainer acknowledges the issue AND at least one clean audit succeeds.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-01: TestClearEligibleQuarantineGatesOnAcknowledgementAndCleanAudit proves expiry alone never lifts a quarantine (acknowledgement plus a clean comparable audit is still required) and that an unexpired quarantine waits out its window even after acknowledgement plus a clean audit.
limitations: Requires PostgreSQL; executes in the CI integration job (no Docker/PostgreSQL on the Windows development host).

requirements.text: It must not auto-clear solely because time passed.
limitations: Clearing requires expiry AND maintainer acknowledgement AND a later clean comparable audit: ClearEligibleQuarantine's SQL (audits.go:211-252) demands an acknowledged row whose window has passed plus a NO_MISS_OBSERVED comparable audit recorded after acknowledgement, and re-quarantining resets the acknowledgement (audits.go:98) - time alone never clears. Direct assertion is CI-only: TestClearEligibleQuarantineGatesOnAcknowledgementAndCleanAudit (quarantine_calibration_integration_test.go:120-178, tag integration) requires PostgreSQL; locally classifier_test.go:41-50 (PASS 2026-11-04) asserts only that an incomparable audit cannot clear a quarantine.

requirements.text: Flakiness does not make a test irrelevant.
limitations: Flaky tests remain selection candidates with a bounded reliability penalty (reliability *= 1 - min(0.25, flakeRate*0.25), planner.go:764-768) and the explanation retains flakiness (:890), but no test supplies a FlakeRate to assert they stay selected with the label.

requirements.text: Store per-test failure/pass counts and classify flakiness only after a minimum number of comparable observations.
implementation: Config key analysis.flake_minimum_comparable_observations (default 5): internal/config/types.go:31, defaults.go:10, validate.go:32-34 (rejects values below 1), schemas/ivp-config.schema.json:11 (integer minimum 1), both shipped templates; organization floor precedence.go:79-81; mapping precedence.go:179.

Threading config -> domain.Policy.FlakeMinimumComparableObservations (internal/domain/policy.go:24) -> read gate Backend.createPlan -> DB.ApplyTestHistory (internal/service/backend.go:327, internal/persistence/history.go:19,61) and write gate submitAudit -> audit Input (backend.go:507,513; internal/audit/classifier.go:66-68) -> RecordAuditAndQuarantine (internal/persistence/audits.go:88-92).

Pure gates: flakeRate (internal/persistence/history.go:78-84) returns 0 below the minimum; flakeClassification (audits.go:161-168) stamps FLAKY only with observations >= minimum while REPEATED stays ungated; comparableObservationCount (audits.go:139-150) counts comparable observations under the read side's identity (integration-only SQL); legacy stored policies normalize to the default at both read paths (backend.go:458-463).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestFlakeRateRequiresMinimumComparableObservations (internal/persistence/history_test.go:9, 10 subtests) - flaky rates below the minimum return 0, exact-at-minimum and above compute the exact rate, zero samples and non-positive minimums fail closed.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestFlakeClassificationGatesFLAKYOnComparableObservations (internal/persistence/audits_test.go:53, 9 subtests) - FLAKY only at/above the minimum, below-minimum flaky repeats write the empty classification (clearing premature insert-time stamps), non-flaky repeats stay REPEATED.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestFlakeMinimumComparableObservationsDefaultValidationAndTemplates (internal/config/config_test.go:387) - default 5, validation of 0 and -1, both shipped templates carry 5, repository may raise the value; schema boundary parity (internal/config/schema_parity_test.go:579-582); full suite go test ./... -count=1 all 26 packages ok, gofmt/vet/vet -tags integration/build green.
limitations: The write-side comparable-observation count is all-time, not windowed by policy.HistoryWindow; the read-side windowed gate still bounds every flake-rate claim that is computed from stamped rows.
The count SQL (comparableObservationCount) is integration-only PostgreSQL and is compile-verified with go vet -tags integration; the classification decision fed to the column is DB-less tested.

REPEATED is intentionally ungated (retry reproducibility, not a flakiness claim), and plans_executions insert-time FLAKY stamps are not gated (their effect on rates is neutralized by the read-side gate).

validateMonotonicPolicy was not extended (it would reject policy JSON from older clients); the organization floor lives in enforceOrganizationConstraints, the load-time path where sibling analysis thresholds are enforced.

requirements.text: A test failure must be re-run according to policy (default: one retry, two total attempts) to distinguish likely flakiness from a reproducible failure.
limitations: Default FailureRetryCount is 1 (defaults.go:22), giving one retry and two total attempts; bounds are 0-3 (validate.go:98-99) and the run loop re-runs a failed test unit up to that count while never retrying checks (run.go:524-527). Bounds are asserted (schema_parity_test.go:564-565) but neither the default value nor the retry loop is - internal/cli has only audit_test.go.

requirements.text: Preserve both results.
limitations: Every attempt is preserved: attemptResults accumulates all runs (run.go:511,524-527), each is appended to local.CommandResults with a per-attempt unit result carrying Attempt: attemptIndex+1 (run.go:533-554), and audit repeats store RepeatCount (audits.go:70-86). No test asserts both results are retained - internal/cli has only audit_test.go.

requirements.text: Any ambiguous failed audit is POSSIBLE_MISS and triggers conservative quarantine until adjudicated.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestPossibleMissQuarantinesUntilHumanResolution (classifier_test.go:52-60) asserts an ambiguous (flaky) full-suite failure classifies as DispositionPossible with Quarantine=true, and TestUnreviewedUnrelatedFailureRemainsPossible (classifier_test.go:73-81) asserts an unreviewed unrelated failure stays POSSIBLE_MISS rather than being dismissed.
limitations: 'Until adjudicated' has no write path: AuditRecord.AdjudicatedAt (domain/types.go:238) is never set anywhere; adjudication is represented only by quarantine acknowledge/clear (audits.go:211-252, PostgreSQL - CI-only). Tracked as strategy section 3.4 gap item 5 (adjudication write path).

requirements.text: Every repository may configure mandatory checks (format, lint, type checking, secret scan, dependency policy, contract checks, compliance, and release checks).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: config_test.go:65-91 asserts organization-mandated check IDs survive the org+repository config merge (union at precedence.go:112), and TestSafetyDefaultsMatchLLDExampleAndShippedTemplates (schema_parity_test.go:487,513-534) asserts safety.always_run_check_ids agrees across the LLD §5.2 example, config.Defaults() and both shipped templates.

requirements.text: They are selected before optimization and are never removed by the optimizer.

requirements.text: The server must verify policy precedence so a repository cannot override a mandatory check in .ivp/config.yaml.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: config_test.go:65-91 asserts a repository config cannot lose organization-mandated check IDs ('mandatory check %q was lost' at config_test.go:79-80) - the repository cannot override a mandatory check in .ivp/config.yaml.

requirements.text: ExecutionCommand contains Executable, Args []string, WorkingDirectory, a strict environment allowlist/map, timeout, resource group, and redaction metadata.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: contract_test.go:57-62 asserts Executable, WorkingDirectory, Timeout and MaxOutputBytes are populated for all seven adapters; runner_test.go:42-56 runs a command carrying an Environment map and asserts secret redaction ([REDACTED]) plus output bounding; runner_test.go:60-73 asserts the Timeout is enforced.

requirements.text: It does not contain a free-form shell command.

requirements.text: Materialize must verify that target keys came from the current snapshot or trusted repository config and reject unknown targets.
evidence: PASS on 2026-10-30: Shared materialization test passed for all seven adapters; unknown snapshot targets were rejected.

requirements.text: All external command outputs are size-limited and parsed as untrusted input.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestReadReportIsBoundedAndContained (reports_test.go:89-103) rejects an oversized report, a path escaping the repository and a partial report set, and runner_test.go:53-56 asserts MaxOutputBytes bounds command stdout (OutputTruncated, excerpt within 1024 bytes).

requirements.text: Adapter parsers MUST handle missing, malformed, oversized, and version-incompatible report files without panic; those failures mark evidence incomplete and trigger safe fallback.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: registry_test.go:26-28 asserts all seven adapters reject a missing report; reports_test.go:21-32 rejects malformed JUnit and flags a zero-test suite; bazel_test.go:20-22 rejects malformed BEP; nx_test.go:24-28 rejects malformed project JSON; reports_test.go:94-96 rejects an oversized report.

requirements.text: Discover Gradle wrapper and project structure; prefer ./gradlew over system Gradle when the wrapper is checked in.
limitations: tool() prefers a checked-in wrapper via FindFirst(root, "gradlew", "gradlew.bat") before falling back to system gradle (gradle.go:24-29), and Detect records which wrapper was chosen (gradle.go:30-36); no test exercises wrapper preference - gradle_test.go covers only the discovery parsers.

requirements.text: Query tasks/projects and identify Test tasks, configured integration test tasks, and required check tasks.
evidence: PASS on 2026-10-30: project/task discovery fixtures identify nested projects and test-like tasks, deduplicate output, and ignore check-only tasks.
limitations: The native Gradle CLI discovery and behavior for required checks have not been executed against a representative Gradle workspace.

requirements.text: Do not assume every task named test has identical semantics.
limitations: Tasks are typed by a name heuristic (parseTestTaskNames keeps any task whose name contains 'test', gradle.go:73-88) that knowingly admits compile-only tasks - gradle_test.go:26 explicitly accepts compileTestJava; ADR 0008 records the choice and the ZERO_TESTS/REPORT_PARSE guard (runner.go:383-388) that protects it, but that guard has no test assertion; tracked as gap section 3.1 item 3.

requirements.text: Represent target keys as :projectPath:taskName.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: contract_test.go:26 materializes the key ":test" for the gradle adapter, gradle_test.go:14 asserts project paths parse as ":api"/":service:worker", and validTaskKey (gradle.go:357-372) enforces the :projectPath:taskName shape.
limitations: Composed multi-segment keys such as ":service:worker:test" are never materialized or asserted end-to-end.

requirements.text: Use Gradle --tests filters only for a Test task where the task supports them; if the task's type/behavior is unknown, execute the whole task.
limitations: --tests filters are appended only when supportsGradleTestFilter accepts the task name (gradle.go:286-291,305-307); otherwise the whole task executes. The gate is unasserted - no test drives Materialize with a non-filterable task name - and the task's true type remains unknown (ADR 0008, gap section 3.1 item 3 open).

requirements.text: Parse JUnit XML reports and JaCoCo XML when present.
evidence: PASS on 2026-10-30: shared JUnit XML and JaCoCo XML parser fixtures passed; Gradle delegates to the tested shared parser.
limitations: Native Gradle report file collection and reports from a real build were not exercised.

requirements.text: Associate coverage with test cases only if test-specific coverage data exists; otherwise use class/file/target-level edges.
limitations: Capabilities declare CoveragePrecision CLASS_OR_FILE (gradle.go:21), so coverage is never claimed per test case, and ValidateCoverageObservation rejects suite-level coverage labeled test-specific (validation.go:122-123) while accepting the FILE precision (validation.go:131-134). Neither rule is asserted by a test, and no Gradle coverage-context data exists to associate.

requirements.text: Do not blindly use Gradle build cache as a substitute for a test result.
limitations: Absence-based: no adapter or runner code invokes the Gradle build cache (grep of internal/adapters finds no cache usage) - every result comes from executing the command and parsing its report (runner.go:341-389). The negative is unasserted, and Gradle's own cache behavior cannot be exercised in this environment.

requirements.text: Respect the build's configured cache behavior and include Gradle version, JVM, wrapper distribution, lockfiles and relevant properties in fingerprints.
limitations: The toolchain fingerprint is a digest of adapter version strings (index.go:465): the Gradle version comes from the first line of `gradlew --version` (gradle.go:37-49) but the JVM version is not extracted (first-line-only).
