Executing the real tools against these fixtures (as opposed to parsing their outputs) remains environment-gated; malformed/truncated/timeout states are modeled at the report/stdout level per each adapter's actual detection mechanism.

requirements.text: exec.CommandContext(executable, args...); no shell by default.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner.go:204 invokes exec.Command(executable, command.Args...) with the argv as an argument array and no shell; runner_test.go:17-30 runs a real child process, runner_test.go:32-58 asserts bounded output plus secret redaction for a command carrying an Environment map, and runner_test.go:83-92 asserts a traversal executable is refused with ErrorClass INVALID_COMMAND.
limitations: The LLD-named exec.CommandContext form is not used literally: runner.go:204 calls exec.Command and couples the context manually (timeout context :210-215, select on ctx.Done with process-group termination :238-266) - context-driven behavior is equivalent but the exact API named in the LLD differs.

requirements.text: Set explicit working directory inside repository; reject path traversal.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: the working directory is resolved through adapters.ResolveWithin (adapter.go:240) at runner.go:197-203 and failures carry ErrorClass WORKING_DIRECTORY (:199); traversal rejection by ResolveWithin is asserted at reports_test.go:75-87 (path escaping the repository refused) and runner_test.go:83-92 refuses a traversal executable.
limitations: The runner's own working-directory use of ResolveWithin (runner.go:197-203) has no direct assertion - traversal is asserted at the report-path call site, not the workdir call site.

requirements.text: Pass only required environment variables.
limitations: The child environment is built exclusively from the allowlist (defaults at :91-92, assembly at :562-576) and a command-specified variable outside the allowlist is refused (:577-580, ErrorClass ENVIRONMENT_REJECTED :172), but no test drives that rejection - runner_test.go never sets a non-allowlisted variable, so the negative path is unasserted.

requirements.text: Never copy all environment variables to telemetry or the API.
limitations: Result (runner.go:58) and LocalReport (outbox.go:24-45) carry no environment field, so no environment dump can reach telemetry or the API, and the server rejects payload keys such as environment, env, command, argv and shell through hasForbiddenKey (server.go:883-897); the adjacent free-form-text rejection is asserted (server_test.go:141-150), but no test asserts that an uploaded report contains no environment data.

requirements.text: Redact configured secret variable names and common credential/token patterns before logging.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:47-52 asserts a secret environment value appears as [REDACTED] in the stdout excerpt and ANSI escape sequences are stripped - sanitize (runner.go:609-633) applies secretName (:606), ansiPattern (:605) and the collected secret values (:584-589).
limitations: The configured credentialPattern (runner.go:607: bearer tokens and api_key/token/password assignments) and the per-command RedactEnv names (runner.go:567-570,587-589) have no test assertion - grep of *_test.go finds no bearer or api-key redaction case.

requirements.text: Start commands in a process group and terminate child processes on timeout/cancellation (platform-specific implementations for supported OSes).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-01: TestInterruptDuringRunPersistsCancelledAndExitsEight builds the real binary, interrupts a mid-flight full-suite command via GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT) on Windows / SIGINT on Unix, and asserts exit 8 plus a persisted report with the CANCELLED failure class; post-run context-bound steps are skipped so the cancelled outcome is never overwritten by an infra failure.
PASS: TestRunnerTimeoutAndWindowsSelectiveRefusal covers timeout-driven child termination in the runner.
limitations: Windows terminates only the direct child process (Process.Kill); grandchildren started by the child are not placed in a job object, so nested process trees may outlive cancellation on Windows.

requirements.text: Stream stdout/stderr to bounded local files; retain only sanitized excerpts and hashes by default.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:53-56 asserts stdout is bounded by MaxOutputBytes (OutputTruncated with the excerpt inside 1024 bytes) and the excerpt is sanitized; capture files are bounded temp files closed and removed after hashing (runner.go:657-740).
limitations: The sha256 output hashes (runner.go:274-275) and the sanitization of stored excerpts (runner.go:272-275) are not asserted directly - only output bounding and excerpt sanitization are checked (runner_test.go:53-56).

requirements.text: Configure per-command timeout, maximum output bytes, concurrency limits, file-descriptor limits where possible, and cancellation behavior.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:60-73 asserts a command timeout yields StatusTimedOut with ErrorClass TIMEOUT, and runner_test.go:53-56 asserts MaxOutputBytes bounds captured output; concurrency is a global semaphore (runner.go:119-120) plus per-ResourceGroup channels (runner.go:128-146).
limitations: No file-descriptor limits are configured anywhere (process_unix.go:12 sets Setpgid only; process_windows.go:11 is a no-op) - the 'fd limits where possible' clause is unimplemented; cancellation behavior (runner.go:238-266) and ResourceGroup grouping have no test assertion.

requirements.text: Capture start/end monotonic times and resource metrics where available.
limitations: UTC wall-clock StartedAt/CompletedAt and elapsed Duration are recorded (runner.go:99-102) but no resource metrics are captured anywhere: ComputeMillis is simply elapsed wall time (run.go:381) and no CPU/memory sampling exists - 'resource metrics where available' is unimplemented; monotonic behavior rests on time.Now() deltas only and nothing here is asserted by a test.

requirements.text: Detect command-not-found, permission errors, OOM/termination signals, timeout, adapter/report parsing failures, and actual test failures as distinct result classes.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:83-92 asserts ErrorClass INVALID_COMMAND for a traversal executable and runner_test.go:60-73 asserts ErrorClass TIMEOUT for an overrunning command - distinct failure modes produce distinct result classes; the full taxonomy (INVALID_COMMAND, COMMAND_NOT_FOUND :163/597, PERMISSION_DENIED :600, REPORT_PARSE :375, ZERO_TESTS :386, PROCESS_EXIT :288, TIMEOUT :219) lives at the cited lines.
limitations: Only INVALID_COMMAND and TIMEOUT are asserted by tests; COMMAND_NOT_FOUND, PERMISSION_DENIED, REPORT_PARSE, ZERO_TESTS and PROCESS_EXIT are unasserted at runner level; OOM/termination-signal detection is not implemented as a distinct class - a signal-killed process surfaces as PROCESS_EXIT/PROCESS_FAILURE (:288-290) with no OOM classification.

requirements.text: A state transition must be persisted locally before a remote status update is attempted.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: TestOutboxPersistsBeforeUploadAndRetriesWithoutExecution (outbox_test.go:13-24) asserts the report is written to the local .ivp/outbox store before any upload attempt is made (Save at outbox.go:62-165, PersistThenUpload at :230-250).

requirements.text: The client uses idempotency keys for result uploads.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: outbox_test.go:20-33 asserts the IdempotencyKey is stored on the LocalReport and remains stable across save and reload, so a retried upload reuses the same key.
limitations: The client-side attachment of the Idempotency-Key header (client.go:152-154) and server-side replay for result uploads specifically are not asserted end-to-end from the CLI - replay is asserted only at the API layer for executions.start (server_test.go:105-121).

requirements.text: Server unavailability must not lose the local report; queue a bounded retry file in .ivp/outbox/, encrypt it if it contains sensitive metadata, and retry safely.
limitations: A bounded retry file lives in .ivp/outbox (NewOutbox bounds at outbox.go:48-61, pruning inside Save) and RetryUploads (outbox.go:166-229, exercised at outbox_test.go:25-43) retries safely without re-execution, but there is no encryption: the report is written as plain JSON (outbox.go:62-165) - the 'encrypt it if it contains sensitive metadata' clause is unimplemented (content is limited to sanitized excerpts and sha256 hashes by construction, runner.go:272-275,657-740).

requirements.text: Do not re-execute tests merely because result upload failed.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: outbox_test.go:25-43 (the retry phase of TestOutboxPersistsBeforeUploadAndRetriesWithoutExecution) asserts a failed upload is retried from the local queue without any command being executed between attempts.

requirements.text: Recompute the relevant worktree fingerprint.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:101-104 asserts ValidatePlan rejects the plan when the recomputed worktree fingerprint differs from plan.WorktreeHash (runner.go:761-763).

requirements.text: Confirm all selected target references still exist.
limitations: ValidatePlan requires a non-nil KnownTargetRefs inventory (:770-772) and rejects any selected target ref absent from the snapshot (:783-785, message 'no longer in the snapshot'), but the only ValidatePlan test (runner_test.go:94-110) never supplies an unknown ref - the existence re-check is unasserted.

requirements.text: Confirm policy version and plan expiration are valid.
limitations: Plan status, expiry (:758-760), policy version (:764-766) and algorithm version (:767-769) are all re-checked by ValidatePlan, but runner_test.go:94-110 only exercises the happy values for these fields - expiry, policy and algorithm rejection are unasserted.

requirements.text: Confirm mandatory checks have not changed.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:106-108 asserts ValidatePlan fails when the current mandatory-check set no longer matches the plan (runner.go:800-804 requires every current mandatory check to be present in the plan's selected/mandatory units).

requirements.text: If any check fails, mark the plan STALE and create a new plan or run full verification.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: TestRunPlanStopsAfterWorktreeMutation (runner_test.go:112-146) asserts a validation failure during execution marks the result StatusStalePlan/OutcomeStale and stops after the first command instead of running the remaining list.
limitations: The run-side stale handling has no test: post-run fingerprint mismatch marks the local result STALE (run.go:622-626) and dry-run rejects a stale plan (run.go:787-789) - internal/cli has only audit_test.go; 'create a new plan or run full verification' after staleness is a user/CI action, not an automatic CLI step.

requirements.text: A selected test filter resolves to zero tests unexpectedly.
limitations: Zero detected tests convert to StatusInfraError + OutcomeInfraFailure with ErrorClass ZERO_TESTS (runner.go:383-388) instead of a pass; adapter parsers do detect zero-test reports (asserted at reports_test.go:21-32) but the runner's conversion and the resulting full-suite escalation have no test assertion.

requirements.text: The adapter cannot parse a result reliably.
limitations: A parse failure, incomplete report or unreliable report yields StatusInfraError + OutcomeInfraFailure with ErrorClass REPORT_PARSE (runner.go:372-381); malformed-input rejection is asserted only at the parser level (reports_test.go:21-32, bazel_test.go:20-22, nx_test.go:24-28) - the runner's conversion wiring is unasserted.

requirements.text: Dependency resolution, test discovery, compilation setup, or test environment initialization fails before tests run.
limitations: Pre-test failures (bad executable path :154, command not found :163, environment rejection :172, output capture :183, report path :192, working directory :199) and process/report failures (:280-296, :350-389) are classified as infra errors rather than test failures, but only INVALID_COMMAND and TIMEOUT have direct assertions (runner_test.go:83-92, :60-73) - the dependency-resolution/discovery/compilation-failure classes have no test.

requirements.text: A selected test reveals a failure and configured policy requires immediate broad diagnosis.
limitations: Broad diagnosis is gated by requiresAuthoritativeComparison (run.go:184-189: OBSERVE mode, or CI fast-feedback with FinalCIFullSuiteRequired) and routed through runPlan's full-suite path (run.go:82-116) plus the isolated audit re-run (audit.go:190-194); no test exercises any of this path (internal/cli has only audit_test.go), and the policy trigger condition itself is configuration-driven.

requirements.text: Execution environment fingerprint differs from plan fingerprint.
implementation: internal/execution/environment.go compares the execution environment fingerprint with the plan fingerprint and refuses the selective execution when they differ; internal/persistence/plans_executions.go stores the environment digest with the execution and downgrades the plan to FULL_REQUIRED.
internal/service/backend.go answers the mismatch with the ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH error and the stored plan requires full verification.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestExecutionStartRejectsChangedEnvironmentFingerprint (internal/service/plan_lifecycle_integration_test.go:213) runs against a real database: a changed environment digest is refused with the ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH error and the stored plan is downgraded to FULL_REQUIRED.
limitations: The comparison happens when the execution starts; a mid-execution environment change is detected by the worktree revalidation, not by a second fingerprint comparison.

requirements.text: A mandatory check was omitted due to configuration mismatch.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:106-108 asserts ValidatePlan rejects a plan that no longer covers the current mandatory-check set (runner.go:800-804: mandatory check %q is missing from the plan), so a configuration-mismatch omission fails validation instead of executing silently.

requirements.text: Any safety-critical data was missing or malformed.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: TestValidateCoverageDoesNotRelabelSuiteCoverageAsPerTest (validation_test.go:36-42) asserts a contradictory coverage observation is rejected with ErrInvalidEvidence, and TestNormalizeRepoPathRequiresCanonicalRepositoryRelativePaths (validation_test.go:10-34) asserts malformed/unsafe paths (../outside, absolute, non-canonical) are rejected - missing or malformed safety-critical data fails closed.
limitations: Most ErrInvalidEvidence branches (snapshot/graph-node/graph-edge/test-unit identity and provenance checks, validation.go:69-160) have no test assertion, and the end-to-end surface (API/CLI returning these errors instead of synthesizing a plan - ADR 0012) is unasserted.

requirements.text: Test assertion failures are genuine verification failures; do not automatically replace them with a full-suite pass.
limitations: A failing targeted run is labeled OutcomeTargetedFail and a failing full run OutcomeFullVerificationFail (runner.go:390-403) - never upgraded to a pass - and the server rejects mislabeled outcomes (plans_executions.go:442-455, CI-only persistence path); no test asserts a failing run's outcome classification: runner_test.go:44 asserts only the passing case (OutcomeFullVerificationPass), and OutcomeTargetedFail appears in tests only as audit-classifier input (classifier_test.go:65).

requirements.text: Record the failing test and allow the developer/agent to fix it.
limitations: The local report written under .ivp/reports (run.go:636-647) carries the structured per-unit results including failing tests, and the outbox keeps it for upload - the developer/agent reads or retrieves it; no test asserts failing-unit details are recorded in the report (internal/cli has only audit_test.go).

requirements.text: A full suite may still run for diagnosis or authoritative CI according to mode.
limitations: Full-suite execution for diagnosis/authoritative CI is decided by mode and force flags (requestedFullSuite = forceFullSuite || PlanFullRequired || ModeFull at run.go:200, fullMode at :123) and requiresAuthoritativeComparison (run.go:184-189); no test exercises mode-driven full-suite selection (internal/cli has only audit_test.go).

requirements.section_title: Why audit is a required product capability
requirements.text: Selective-test planners can look effective by running fewer tests while silently missing relevant failures.
limitations: Rationale statement for the audit capability rather than a directly testable behavior: the miss-measuring engine it motivates exists (internal/audit - Classify compares selected execution against full-suite evidence, asserted by classifier_test.go:30-91, PASS 2026-11-04).

requirements.section_title: Why audit is a required product capability
requirements.text: IVP must continuously measure these misses by comparing selected execution with full-suite evidence on equivalent source and environment snapshots.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: classifier_test.go:30-91 drives six audits that compare a selected-run outcome with full-suite failures and assert the recorded outcomes (CONFIRMED_MISS/POSSIBLE_MISS/NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE/INCOMPARABLE/NO_MISS_OBSERVED); equivalence requires all seven source/environment fingerprints to match (Fingerprint.Equivalent, classifier.go:21-29).
limitations: 'Continuously' is not implemented - audits are submit-driven with no scheduled orchestration (strategy section 3.4 item 3); persistence of comparisons and the Prometheus audit counters (metrics.go:33-34 via service.go:49-53) are unasserted (PostgreSQL path - CI-only).

requirements.text: Observe mode: full suite is always run; planned subset outcome is compared where possible.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: schema_parity_test.go:569 ('observe without full suite rejected') asserts Validate rejects OBSERVE without execute_full_suite - 'OBSERVE always runs the authoritative full suite' (validate.go:48-49) - and the default is ExecuteFullSuite:true (defaults.go:14).
limitations: The OBSERVE execution path (run.go:185,200) is untested (internal/cli has only audit_test.go), and 'planned subset outcome is compared where possible' is asserted only mode-independently by the audit classifier (classifier_test.go:30-91), not through an OBSERVE run.

requirements.text: Fast-feedback mode: selected checks run immediately; full CI remains required.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: schema_parity_test.go:570 ('fast feedback without final CI gate rejected') asserts Validate rejects FAST_FEEDBACK without final_ci_full_suite_required - 'FAST_FEEDBACK never replaces the final CI full suite' (validate.go:51-52) - and planner_test.go:28-29 asserts the FAST_FEEDBACK explanation distinguishes TARGETED_PASS from full-suite outcomes.
limitations: 'Selected checks run immediately' is an execution claim with no test (internal/cli has only audit_test.go), and the runtime final-CI gate (run.go:184-189, requires the CI environment) is unasserted.

requirements.text: An optional isolated background audit can run on a sample of local/CI tasks.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestAuditSampleRateIsScopedToPlanMode (audit_test.go:14-35) asserts each mode's sampling rate source (RISK_BASED_CI uses modes.risk_based_ci.audit_sample_rate, every other mode safety.audit.sample_rate) and TestAuditSampleSelectedIsDeterministicAndBounded (audit_test.go:39-56) asserts the sampling decision is deterministic and bounded - audits run only on a sample of tasks.
limitations: The isolated background workspace execution (createAuditWorkspace, audit.go:427; message at audit.go:115) has no test - it runs a full suite in a temporary workspace and cannot run in unit tests - and server-side audit comparison requires PostgreSQL (CI-only).

requirements.text: Risk-based CI mode: a configurable sample of eligible selective runs receives an authoritative full-suite audit in an isolated worktree/container using the same commit and equivalent toolchain.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-01: TestAuditSampleRateIsScopedToPlanMode proves the configurable RISK_BASED_CI sample rate is read from modes.risk_based_ci.audit_sample_rate instead of the general safety rate; TestAuditSampleSelectedIsDeterministicAndBounded proves re-sampling the same execution is stable and bounded.
limitations: Evidence covers the sampling decision; the isolated-worktree audit full-suite execution itself has no end-to-end regression test in this wave.

requirements.text: Scheduled audit: each repository must run full verification at least according to configured cadence (default daily for active repositories and every release build) even if no random audit was sampled.
implementation: internal/config/types.go:118-129 and internal/config/defaults.go:38 add the scheduled-audit cadence (safety.audit.scheduled_cadence_hours, default 24) and the acknowledgement SLA (safety.audit.acknowledgement_sla_hours, default 24) with validation and the schema/template/parity wiring.

internal/persistence/audit_schedule.go ScheduledAuditRepositories lists every repository with the completion time of its last FULL-mode execution, and UnacknowledgedMisses reports the unacknowledged misses and the age of the oldest one.

internal/service/calibration.go scheduledAuditState/scheduledAuditDue compute the LLD 10.2 due state; internal/service/backend.go forces a plan to FULL verification when the scheduled audit is due, and the metrics repository response carries the schedule state.
internal/audit/schedule.go:16-70 holds the effective schedule policy (cadence, SLA) with the due and overdue decisions.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestSchedulePolicyDecidesDueRunsAndOverdueMisses (internal/audit/metrics_test.go) asserts a repository inside the cadence is not due, one past the cadence is due, one that never ran a full verification is due immediately, an unacknowledged miss past the SLA is overdue and an acknowledged one is not.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestScheduledAuditRepositoriesAndUnacknowledgedMisses (internal/persistence/audit_schedule_integration_test.go:15) runs against a real PostgreSQL: the verified repository reports its last full verification, the fresh one reports none, the unacknowledged quarantine is counted with its age, and acknowledging it clears the signal.
limitations: The cadence and the SLA are policy-level configuration, not per-repository overrides.
The due state is reported per repository; the repository that must run the full verification is the executor's responsibility once the server reports the plan as FULL_REQUIRED.

requirements.text: An audit is comparable only if source tree hash, dependency lockfiles, build/test configuration, tool versions, environment class, and required services match.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: equivalentFingerprints (classifier_test.go:12-15) builds fingerprints matching on all seven fields, TestIncomparableAuditCannotClearQuarantine (classifier_test.go:41-50) asserts that changing a single digest (ToolchainDigest) breaks equivalence and yields INCOMPARABLE, and Fingerprint.Equivalent (classifier.go:21-29) requires all seven fields non-empty and equal; server_test.go:152-167 requires complete fingerprint evidence on audits.submit.
limitations: Only the ToolchainDigest field is exercised by a mismatch test; dependency, build-config, test-config, environment-class and required-services mismatches flow through the same code path but are not individually asserted.

requirements.text: Different data, dependency resolution, test order, nondeterminism or missing reports makes it INCOMPARABLE; it must not be treated as a clean audit.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: classifier_test.go:41-50 asserts a source/toolchain data mismatch classifies as DispositionIncomparable with Record.Outcome=INCOMPARABLE and never as a clean audit (it cannot clear a quarantine).
limitations: Missing reports are classified POSSIBLE_MISS rather than INCOMPARABLE when the full suite fails without an attributable unit (classifier.go:110-118) - still non-clean and conservatively quarantining, but a documented deviation from LLD §10.3; test-order and nondeterminism have no separate classification (they surface only through fingerprint mismatch or flaky failures) and those paths are unasserted.

requirements.text: CONFIRMED_MISS: reproducible failure omitted by selection, plausibly related to the change.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestConfirmedOmittedFailureQuarantines (classifier_test.go:30-39) asserts a Reproduced+RelatedToChange failure omitted from the selected set classifies as DispositionConfirmed with Record.Outcome=CONFIRMED_MISS and exactly one missed test key.

requirements.text: POSSIBLE_MISS: full-suite failure not selected, but evidence is ambiguous/flaky.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestPossibleMissQuarantinesUntilHumanResolution (classifier_test.go:52-60) asserts an ambiguous (flaky) failure classifies as DispositionPossible/POSSIBLE_MISS, and TestUnreviewedUnrelatedFailureRemainsPossible (classifier_test.go:73-81) asserts an unreviewed unrelated failure stays POSSIBLE_MISS.

requirements.text: NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE: test failure demonstrably unrelated to change under reviewed policy.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestReviewedUnrelatedFailureIsNotMiss (classifier_test.go:83-91) asserts a failure marked ReviewedNotAttributable and unrelated to the change classifies as DispositionNotAttributable with no quarantine and Record.Outcome=NO_MISS_OBSERVED.
limitations: The classification is exposed as Disposition NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE (classifier.go:158) but the persisted AuditRecord.Outcome is NO_MISS_OBSERVED (classifier.go:159) - domain.AuditOutcome has no NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE value, so the disposition does not surface as a distinct record outcome.

requirements.text: INCOMPARABLE: snapshot/environment mismatch.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestIncomparableAuditCannotClearQuarantine (classifier_test.go:41-50) asserts a snapshot/environment fingerprint mismatch classifies as DispositionIncomparable with Record.Outcome=INCOMPARABLE and no quarantine clearing.

requirements.text: The system may not autonomously downgrade a POSSIBLE_MISS to NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE without a documented human/CI rule.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestUnreviewedUnrelatedFailureRemainsPossible (classifier_test.go:73-81) asserts an unrelated failure without review stays POSSIBLE_MISS (no autonomous downgrade), while TestReviewedUnrelatedFailureIsNotMiss (classifier_test.go:83-91) asserts the downgrade to NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE happens only when the ReviewedNotAttributable flag is set.
limitations: The 'documented human/CI rule' is the client-supplied ReviewedNotAttributable flag in the audit payload: the server verifies failure evidence against the persisted full execution (audits.go:61 verifyAuditUnitEvidence) but not review provenance, and there is no rule registry or audit-log of the review decision.

requirements.text: Set repository/adapter/rule scope to QUARANTINED.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: classifier_test.go:30-39 and classifier_test.go:52-60 assert the quarantine decision (Quarantine=true) for confirmed and unresolved misses, and audits.go:29 derives the scope key from adapter+rule scope for the QUARANTINED row.
limitations: The QUARANTINED row insert (audits.go:95-98) runs only in the PostgreSQL path - CI-only; scope covers repository (column) plus adapter/rule (scope_key) but there is no risk-level scope dimension (quarantineScope takes adapter and rule only).

requirements.text: Disable selective final-CI gating for that scope and force the full suite.
limitations: An active quarantine escalates the plan to FULL_REQUIRED (policy.Quarantined -> EscQuarantineActive, planner.go:174-177), disabling selective final-CI gating for that scope. No local test asserts it (no test sets policy.Quarantined); gating is covered only by TestExpiredQuarantineStillGatesUntilCleared (internal/service/quarantine_gating_integration_test.go:52, tag integration) which requires PostgreSQL - CI-only.

requirements.text: Record missed tests, selected set, graph evidence, policy, and the failure output hash.
limitations: The audit record stores missed test keys (missed_test_keys_json, audits.go:67) and details_json with adapter, scope, disposition, both fingerprints, failures and failure_output_hash (audits.go:37), with the selected set reachable through execution_id/plan and verified against persisted plan units (audits.go:118,154). Graph evidence and policy are not recorded in the record, and no test asserts the stored fields (PostgreSQL path - CI-only).

requirements.text: Open a machine-readable incident record; provide report output for CI to publish.
limitations: A machine-readable audit record row (audits.go:67) and a machine-readable quarantine.create event (audits.go:102) are opened, and ivp audit prints a disposition line for operators (audit.go:297). There is no incident record type and no report artifact for CI to publish anywhere ('incident' does not appear in the codebase), and no test asserts the output.

requirements.text: Require maintainer acknowledgement and a clean audit before lifting quarantine.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-01: TestClearEligibleQuarantineGatesOnAcknowledgementAndCleanAudit covers all four eligibility gates (unacknowledged, acknowledged without a clean comparable audit, unexpired, expired but unacknowledged) plus the reachable clear path for a never-expiring quarantine.
limitations: Requires PostgreSQL; executes in the CI integration job (no Docker/PostgreSQL on the Windows development host).

requirements.text: Keep historical miss data for quality dashboards.
limitations: Audit records are retained and read back through GetRepositoryMetrics (90-day window with daily comparable/incomparable/miss breakdowns, reads.go:140-253) served at GET /repositories/{id}/metrics (server.go:266) for quality dashboards. Requires PostgreSQL - CI-only; no local test asserts the query results.

requirements.text: Do not erase a miss after changing the policy.
limitations: audit_records is append-only: the persistence layer only INSERTs (audits.go:67) and SELECTs - no DELETE or UPDATE path exists for audit records, and policy updates (backend.go monotonic policy versions) never touch them, so a recorded miss survives policy changes. This is an absence-based guarantee with no test, and it runs only in the PostgreSQL path (CI-only).

requirements.text: Runtime reduction: 1 - selected_runtime/full_runtime for comparable runs.
implementation: internal/audit/metrics.go:111-130 RuntimeReduction computes 1 - selected_runtime/full_runtime over the comparable runs, with the sample size and an explicit no-data state.
internal/persistence/audit_schedule.go CalibrationEvidence gathers the comparable selective/full execution pairs (audit records recorded as comparable) with their runtime and compute.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestCalibrationMetricsComputeFromEvidence/runtime reduction (internal/audit/metrics_test.go:12) asserts the metric equals 0.75 over two comparable runs with the summed denominator, that a run without a measured full-suite runtime is excluded rather than counted as zero, and that no evidence yields an undefined metric with a no-data reason instead of a measured zero.
limitations: Only runs the audit recorded as comparable contribute; an incomparable run is excluded from both sides of the ratio.

requirements.text: Compute reduction: 1 - selected_cpu/full_cpu where CPU metrics exist.

evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestCalibrationMetricsComputeFromEvidence/compute reduction (internal/audit/metrics_test.go:60) asserts the metric equals 0.75 over two measurable runs, that a run without CPU metrics is excluded from numerator and denominator, and that no evidence yields an undefined metric.
limitations: Runs without CPU measurements are excluded from both sides rather than counted as zero CPU.

evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestCalibrationMetricsComputeFromEvidence/regression recall (internal/audit/metrics_test.go:78) asserts the metric is 2/3 when two of three relevant failures were missed and the fourth observed failure was reviewed as unrelated, and that no evidence yields an undefined metric.

requirements.text: Results are append-only; correcting an incorrectly parsed outcome creates a superseding record with an audit reason, never silently overwrites history.
implementation: internal/persistence/migrations/006_result_corrections.sql adds the append-only correction table (execution, test unit key, attempt, superseded status, superseding status, mandatory audit reason, corrected_by, created_at) with its index, the immutable-row trigger and the tenant-isolation policy, so a correction can be added but never changed or deleted.

internal/persistence/corrections.go:32-77 RecordResultCorrection appends a superseding record: it reads the stored result row to capture the status it supersedes, refuses a correction that does not change the status, requires a unit key, a positive attempt, a superseding status and an audit reason, and never updates or deletes the original row (LLD 12.4).

internal/persistence/corrections.go:79-104 ApplyResultCorrections computes the effective results: for every corrected (test unit, attempt) the latest correction supersedes the recorded status, the superseded status and the audit reason stay visible on the result, and the stored rows are never mutated; correctionIsNewer breaks ties deterministically.

internal/persistence/reads.go:120-168 GetExecutionUnitResults loads the corrections of an execution alongside the results and returns the effective, corrected view; internal/persistence/plans_executions.go:161-175 UnitResult carries SupersededStatus and CorrectionReason so a corrected outcome is never indistinguishable from an original one.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestApplyResultCorrectionsKeepsHistoryAndSupersedesStatus (internal/persistence/corrections_test.go:12) asserts that a correction supersedes the effective status of exactly that (test unit, attempt) while the original status and the audit reason stay visible, that an uncorrected result and another attempt of the same unit stay untouched, and that the stored results are not mutated.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestLatestCorrectionForAResultWins (internal/persistence/corrections_test.go:44) asserts that the latest correction wins and that corrections recorded at the same instant break deterministically; TestCorrectionRequiresUnitAttemptStatusAndReason (internal/persistence/corrections_test.go:71) asserts that a correction without a unit key, attempt, superseding status or audit reason is rejected before it reaches the database.
limitations: The correction mechanism is implemented in the persistence layer (migration, append-only table, write path and effective read view); no HTTP or CLI entry point exposes a correction yet, so corrections are recorded by the server-side maintenance path and the API surface is unchanged.

requirements.text: precompute adjacency lists by edge type and connected target/module mappings;
implementation: internal/analysis/derived_index.go:29-66 DerivedIndex carries the adjacency lists by edge type (ReverseDeps for dependency consumers, ReverseCoverage for tests covering a node, DependencyAdj for consumer -> dependency, ContractConsumers for contract consumers) plus the connected target/module mappings (ConnectedTargets, connected in both directions so a lookup never misses a neighbour).

internal/analysis/derived_index.go:104-136 BuildDerivedIndex derives the index once per snapshot from the immutable raw graph; the raw graph stays the source of truth and the index never overrides it. internal/analysis/graph.go:27-140 AnalyzeImpactIndexed consumes the index instead of rebuilding the adjacency maps per request.
internal/analysis/derived_index.go:138-158 sortAll makes every adjacency list deterministic, so a derived index and every plan built from it are byte-stable for identical inputs.
ADR 0021 (docs/adr/0021-derived-graph-index-and-traversal-bounds.md) records the decision and its alternatives.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestDerivedIndexCarriesAdjacencyAndAffectedTargets (internal/analysis/derived_index_test.go:12) asserts the adjacency lists by edge type on a four-node graph - the reverse dependency list of a source file names its build-target consumer, the reverse dependency list of that build target names its test-target consumer, the dependency adjacency of the test target names the build target, the coverage adjacency names the covering test, and the contract-consumer list names the contract's consumer.

PASS on 2026-11-12: TestDerivedIndexIsCachedBySnapshotHashAndAlgorithmVersion (internal/analysis/derived_index_test.go:70) asserts that the index for one snapshot hash is reused (the same instance is returned and the cache grows by exactly one entry), that a different snapshot hash produces a different index and a different cache key, and that a graph that does not match the cached entry is never served from it even when the node and edge counts are identical.
limitations: The derived index is an in-process cache over the immutable raw graph, not a SQL materialized view: it saves the per-request rebuild but does not reduce the rows stored in PostgreSQL (ADR 0021 decision 1).
The index holds adjacency for the edge types the analysis understands (dependency, coverage, contract consumer); other convention edges are not indexed because no traversal consumes them yet.
The cache is bounded to eight entries with least-recently-used eviction, so a process that plans against more than eight snapshots rebuilds the evicted index.

requirements.text: generate an affected-target index for common source->target queries;
implementation: internal/analysis/derived_index.go:104-136 the derived index materializes the affected-target index: for every build/test target it walks the dependency adjacency once and records the source files the target reaches, so AffectedTargets maps a source path to the affected build/test target keys (the common source -> target query).

internal/analysis/derived_index.go:110-136 the closure is computed from the target side, so its cost follows the number of targets rather than the number of files; the result is deduplicated and sorted by sortAll (derived_index.go:138-158).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestDerivedIndexCarriesAdjacencyAndAffectedTargets (internal/analysis/derived_index_test.go:12) asserts that the affected-target index maps the source path 'src/app.go' to both targets that depend on it ('build:app' and 'test:app', transitively) and that the connected target mapping for 'build:app' names both of its neighbours while 'test:app' names 'build:app'.

PASS on 2026-11-12: the full suite (go test ./... -count=1) is green, so the index is used by the planner without changing any plan outcome - the plans stay byte-identical for identical inputs because the adjacency lists are sorted.
limitations: The index is built from the dependency edges of the snapshot; a source file that is not reachable from any build/test target has no entry (the query answers 'no affected target', not 'unknown').
Only build, test and check targets are indexed as affected targets; other node types (services, owners, generated outputs) are not target candidates for this query.
The index is per snapshot: a change to the graph invalidates it through the cache's content fingerprint, and a new snapshot gets its own index.

requirements.text: store the immutable raw graph as source of truth;
limitations: The raw graph tables are stored as immutable source of truth: graph_nodes/graph_edges are covered by the immutable_row BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger (001_init.sql:189-190) raised by ivp_reject_immutable_mutation (:166-184), so mutations beyond append are rejected; but the trigger's enforcement is DDL that can only be asserted by the CI-only migration test (postgres_integration_test.go:18, ci.yml:93) - no local execution evidence.

requirements.text: cache read-only derived index by snapshot hash and algorithm version.
implementation: internal/analysis/derived_index.go:161-215 the read-only derived index is cached by snapshot hash and algorithm version (DerivedIndexKey), with a bounded LRU cache (eight entries, least-recently-used eviction) so a long-lived process cannot grow without limit.

internal/analysis/derived_index.go:180-215 a cached index is reused only when its content fingerprint still matches the graph it is asked about; the fingerprint is order-independent over the node identities and the edge endpoints and types, so a snapshot hash that cannot identify its content can never yield a wrong index (ADR 0021 decision 2).

internal/analysis/planner.go:247-250 the planner obtains the index through DerivedIndexFor(evidence.Snapshot.TreeHash, ...) and passes it to AnalyzeImpactIndexed, so every plan against the same snapshot reuses one derivation.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestDerivedIndexIsCachedBySnapshotHashAndAlgorithmVersion (internal/analysis/derived_index_test.go:70) asserts the caching contract directly - the same snapshot hash returns the identical index instance, the cache entry count grows by exactly one for a new snapshot, a different snapshot hash produces a different index and a different cache key, and a graph that differs from the cached one is never served from the cache even with identical node and edge counts.

PASS on 2026-11-12: DerivedIndexKey composes the snapshot hash and the algorithm version, so an index built by a different planner algorithm version is never reused; the planner calls DerivedIndexFor for every plan (internal/analysis/planner.go:250).
limitations: The cache is per process: a restart or another replica rebuilds the index, and the cache is not shared between the CLI and the server.
The cache is bounded to eight entries with least-recently-used eviction; a workload that plans against more than eight snapshots in rotation rebuilds the evicted indexes.
The derived index is read-only by construction: it is derived from the immutable raw graph and never written back, so a stale snapshot can never poison it.

requirements.text: Artifact sanitizer strips ANSI terminal codes, control characters, known token/key patterns and truncates output; sanitization is best-effort and is not a reason to upload arbitrary logs by default.
evidence: PASS on 2026-10-30: full Go suite passed; sanitizer fixtures verify ANSI, secrets, source paths, and freeform failure/log removal.

requirements.text: CLI logs only the names of environment variables, never their values.
limitations: Absence-based: no code path logs environment values (grep os.Environ() finds no matches; the child environment is assembled only as the exec envp array NAME=value (runner.go:583-589), and secret values are collected solely for redaction (:584-589, sanitize :605-633)); no test asserts the no-values-logged property.

requirements.text: Explicitly denylist *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, *_PASSWORD, cloud credentials and provider keys.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: runner_test.go:47-52 asserts a secret-named environment value appears as [REDACTED] in the captured excerpt; the denylist secretName (runner.go:606) matches case-insensitive TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|API.?KEY|PRIVATE.?KEY|CREDENTIAL|AUTH - covering *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, *_PASSWORD, api/private keys and cloud credential names.
limitations: Only one representative secret name is asserted (runner_test.go:47-52); names containing none of the denylist substrings (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID) are not matched by secretName, and per-command RedactEnv additions (runner.go:567-570,587-589) are unasserted.

requirements.text: Do not use a shared cache for command output that may contain tenant data.
limitations: No shared cache for command output exists (absence-based: grep finds no cross-run output cache); output is captured in per-run bounded temp files that are closed and removed after hashing (runner.go:657-740), leaving only sanitized excerpts/hashes; unasserted - no test inspects capture-file lifecycle.

requirements.text: If shared artifact storage is enabled, enforce tenant-specific keys and access checks.
evidence: PASS on 2026-10-30: service/API/store tests passed, including cross-tenant retrieval denial, tenant-derived object keys, and role checks.
limitations: Database-backed tenant isolation is awaiting the PostgreSQL integration target.

requirements.text: Run repo tools with the caller's permissions and optional container/sandbox profiles; never run builds as root in CI containers.
limitations: The image never runs as root: FROM scratch with USER 65532:65532 (Dockerfile:20,24) and a digest-pinned build base (:2); child processes run with the caller's permissions - the runner performs no privilege elevation (runner.go:99-146); but optional container/sandbox profiles are not configurable anywhere (no sandbox profile setting exists), and no test asserts the runtime identity of builds.

requirements.text: Restrict generic adapter executables to allowlisted paths.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: TestGenericRejectsShellInjectionAndTraversal (generic_test.go:32-59) includes the case 'unallowlisted binary' (:42) - `sh -c` with an empty AllowedExecutables - and asserts Materialize refuses it ('unsafe command/path accepted' at :55), alongside shell-substitution (:40) and path-traversal (:41) refusal; allowlist checks live at generic.go:73,123,243.
limitations: The restriction is by executable name (AllowedExecutables), not by filesystem path as the LLD wording says; and every production call site passes a nil allowlist (config/adapter.go:11-16; callers cli.go:89,136, index.go:124, run.go:769), so the end-to-end CLI behavior with the trusted-policy allowlist is unasserted.

requirements.text: Config changes from untrusted pull requests cannot grant new executables or disable policy gates unless a trusted owner approves the change.
limitations: The executable allowlist is supplied by trusted policy, never repository YAML (config/adapter.go:9-16 comment; all ToAdapterConfig call sites pass nil, so repo config cannot grant executables); policy gates ride on server-signed policy (signature verification on the policy path, org-bounds enforced at backend.go:517) and policy updates require the maintainer role (server.go:257); but no test asserts the pull-request scenario itself - an untrusted PR attempting to grant executables or disable a gate - and 'trusted owner approval' is enforced only via signed policy + role gate, not an explicit approval workflow.

requirements.text: Apply request body size limits, query timeout limits, rate limits, output caps, and pagination to mitigate denial-of-service.
limitations: Body size limit (24 MiB default, server.go:208,220), rate limiting (25 rps/burst 50, :210-219), pagination validation (:317-323, :831), strict payload caps (readPayload :527) and runner output/concurrency caps (runner.go:43-56,118-146) exist; MISSING: no statement/query timeouts anywhere (grep statement_timeout|QueryTimeout = no matches), no pagination for unit-result listing, no rate-limit TTL/cleanup, and the server never emits Retry-After - tracked as strategy section 3.4 item 8; none of the present limits is asserted by a test.

requirements.text: Publish SBOM, scan dependencies/container images, sign release artifacts, and verify artifact checksums in installation instructions.
limitations: SBOM generation plus govulncheck (ci.yml:103-110), Trivy image scanning (release.yml:76-78) and cosign sign+verify (release.yml:104-115) are configured; MISSING: installation instructions contain no artifact checksums (grep sha256sum|checksum over README.md/docs finds only the LLD requirement text at LLD line 902) - the 'verify artifact checksums in installation instructions' clause is unimplemented; the workflows themselves have no execution evidence from this host.

requirements.text: Audit all policy edits, quarantine changes, audit adjudications and privilege changes.

implementation: internal/domain/upgrade.go holds the upgrade state (algorithm version, policy version, reset time and the calibration counters observed at the reset); internal/persistence/upgrade_state.go stores it per repository.
internal/service/plan_gates.go effectivePlanMode resets a RISK_BASED_CI request to OBSERVE while the repository is not re-calibrated; internal/service/backend.go observes the upgrade on every plan.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: TestRiskBasedCIResetsToObserveAfterMajorPolicyChange (internal/service/plan_lifecycle_integration_test.go:246) asserts against a real database that a new policy version resets the selective eligibility to OBSERVE until the repository is re-calibrated, and that a request without a reset keeps its mode.
limitations: The reset applies to RISK_BASED_CI requests; the other modes are unaffected because their eligibility is not calibration-gated.

requirements.text: Selection conservatism beats theoretical minimality.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: conservative escalation beats smaller selections - stale fingerprint/policy forces FULL_REQUIRED (planner_test.go:41-61), hard path and dangling graph force full verification (:63-88), and a selection without runtime advantage escalates instead of taking the smaller plan (:188-199).
limitations: Dynamic/reflection risk labels that should also force conservatism are never populated (strategy section 3.2 item 2), so part of the conservative rule set is dormant in production paths; assertions cover only the exercised rules.

requirements.text: The objective is minimum sufficient verification supported by evidence, not the smallest number of tests.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: selective plans must clear evidence gates - weighted coverage >= risk-tier threshold and confidence >= 0.98 (planner_test.go:25-26), mandatory checks are always included or the plan escalates (:110-149), and runtime-budget exhaustion escalates rather than shrinking the set (:188-199).
limitations: Asserted through the exercised gate scenarios only; no test enumerates 'sufficient evidence' boundaries per risk tier, and dormant risk-label rules (strategy section 3.2 item 2) leave part of the evidence requirement unenforced in production paths.

requirements.text: A graph is only as good as its evidence.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: incomplete or invalid evidence cannot yield a targeted plan - a dangling graph edge forces FULL_REQUIRED (planner_test.go:76-87), suite-level coverage cannot masquerade as test-specific evidence (validation_test.go:36-42), and READY plans must clear the evidence-driven confidence gate (planner_test.go:25-26).
limitations: The EscGraphStale escalation for aged evidence (planner.go:147-150) has no direct test (only stale fingerprint and dangling-edge paths are asserted), and evidence-confidence scoring internals are gated end-to-end only.

requirements.text: Missing dynamic/reflection/runtime dependencies reduce confidence and trigger escalation.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: absent graph evidence forces conservatism rather than confidence - a dangling dependency edge escalates to FULL_REQUIRED (planner_test.go:76-87), and a READY plan must clear the minimum selection confidence gate of 0.98 (planner_test.go:25-26).
limitations: Dynamic dispatch/reflection dependencies are not modeled at all: DetectedRiskLabels are never populated by `ivp index` (strategy section 3.2 item 2), so the specific 'missing dynamic/reflection dependency' trigger has no implementation to test; no test varies confidence under missing dynamic edges.

requirements.text: Coverage is not a complete dependency map.
implementation: internal/analysis/planner.go:238,345-361,392,947 (coverage one input among graph/history/risk; mandatory always-run)
limitations: Selection combines weighted coverage with DEPENDS_ON/TEST_COVERS traversal, risk scoring and mandatory status - coverage is only one input and mandatory units run regardless of coverage (planner.go:392,947); but no direct test asserts that non-coverage inputs independently force inclusion (mandatory inclusion is validated only through the runner required-checks list, runner_test.go:106-108).

requirements.text: A test's past execution coverage may not expose every behavioral dependency or integration-level failure.
implementation: internal/analysis/planner.go:351 (calculateConfidence combines coverage, graph completeness and history)
limitations: Past execution coverage cannot satisfy the plan alone: confidence combines coverage with graph completeness and history (planner.go:351), risk scoring penalizes evidence gaps and rewards regression history (risk.go:79-94), and coverage staleness escalates when trusted mappings are insufficient (planner.go:370-371); but no test asserts that a behavioral dependency missing from coverage is compensated by graph/history inputs.

requirements.text: Build-system graphs are not interchangeable.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: each adapter parses its own graph semantics with dedicated fixtures - Maven reactor/Failsafe discovery and escaping-module incompleteness (maven_test.go:24,47), Gradle project/task parsers (gradle_test.go:8), Nx project edges (nx_test.go:8,30), Bazel BEP targets (bazel_test.go:5), pytest node-level collection (pytest_test.go:8,27) - per ADR 0007 (maven) and ADR 0008 (gradle).
limitations: Tests assert each parser's own fixture behavior; no test asserts the non-interchangeability principle itself (e.g. that a Maven reactor relation is never interpreted as a Gradle task edge), and fixtures are inline literals (strategy section 3.1 item 1).

requirements.text: Maven reactor dependency relations, Gradle configured tasks, Bazel configured targets and Nx project edges have different semantics.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: semantics are asserted per build system - Maven reactor module graph and Failsafe split (maven_test.go:24), escaping reactor module marked incomplete (:47), Gradle configured project/task fixtures (gradle_test.go:8), Nx project edges with Jest configuration (nx_test.go:30), and Bazel configured targets via BEP (bazel_test.go:5).
limitations: There is no shared contract asserting these relation types are normalized differently rather than interchangeably - the equivalent-outcome contract test (strategy section 3.1 item 2) is still open, and all fixtures are inline.

requirements.text: Keep adapter-specific semantics and normalize only after preserving provenance.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: TestDomainUnitPreservesAdapterMetadata (domain_test.go:11) asserts adapter-provided metadata (display name, runner, report/coverage paths, dependencies) survives conversion into domain units, keeping provenance next to the normalized fields.
limitations: Assertion covers metadata passthrough in one conversion path; which adapter/format produced a given parsed result is not asserted end-to-end, and cross-adapter normalization equivalence has no contract test (strategy section 3.1 item 2).

requirements.text: Test duration estimates are uncertain.
limitations: Estimates are treated as uncertain: P95 is preferred when >=5 samples exist (planner.go:1016-1017), unknown durations hurt confidence (planner.go:424), and history loads p50/p95/sample counts via percentile_disc (history.go:29-30); but no test asserts the uncertain-estimate behavior (the runtime-budget test uses fixed estimates, planner_test.go:188-199) and no plan-level uncertainty interval is computed - tracked as strategy section 3.2 item 13.

requirements.text: Prefer P95 and report uncertainty; do not select a cheaper plan based on optimistic means alone.
limitations: P95 is preferred over means at unit-estimate level (planner.go:1016-1017 guards on DurationSampleCount >= 5 and DurationP95Millis > 0, so optimistic means are never used when P95 exists) and percentile_disc(0.95) computes it from history (history.go:30); but no plan-level uncertainty interval is reported (strategy section 3.2 item 13, tracked as row IVP-6-2-fd59dc2ae2) and no test asserts the P95-vs-mean choice.

requirements.text: Tests may be order-dependent or share resources.
limitations: Resource groups flow from adapter discovery through plan units to materialized commands (run.go:1440) and the runner serializes commands in the same ResourceGroup through a capacity-1 channel (runner.go:128-138); execution is sequential in plan order (scheduler.go:60-101), so shared-resource isolation holds by construction - but no test runs grouped commands, and order-dependence detection itself does not exist.

requirements.text: Execution grouping/resource leases must preserve required serial order and isolation.
limitations: Required serial order is preserved by the sequential plan-order loop (scheduler.go:60-101) and group isolation by the capacity-1 ResourceGroup channel (runner.go:128-138); but no test asserts that order-dependent units run in their required order or that groups isolate resources (no grouped-command test exists), and the concurrency semaphore's interaction with groups is unasserted.

requirements.text: Caching is not the primary IVP responsibility.
limitations: Absence-based: IVP implements no plan/result cache of its own (grep of *.go finds no cache layer; every request rebuilds traversal state, graph.go:12-117) and plan reuse goes through immutable persisted snapshots instead; unasserted - there is no cache behavior to test.

requirements.text: Use native build caches; IVP may read their telemetry but must not duplicate or weaken them.
limitations: Absence-based: no adapter injects cache-disabling flags or wraps native caches - materialize keeps adapter argv as configured (asserted by TestMaterializeKeepsArgvAndExpandsWholeArgumentPlaceholders, generic_test.go:12-25), and IVP does not read native cache telemetry either; no test asserts caches were left untouched.

requirements.text: A passing targeted run is not a passing complete suite.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: the plan explanation distinguishes TARGETED_PASS from full-suite claims ('nothing about unselected tests', planner_test.go:28-29), and the audit classifier only reports a miss when an equivalent full run fails after a passing selected run (classifier_test.go:30-39 confirmed miss, :62-71 failing selected run is not a miss); ADR 0005 records the semantics.
limitations: CLI rendering of this distinction has no test (internal/cli has only audit_test.go), and no API/dashboard assertion checks the outcome label text.

requirements.text: CLI, API, dashboards and CI annotations must preserve this semantic difference.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: explanation content distinguishing selective from full outcomes is asserted (planner_test.go:28-29), and metrics tests assert outcome-labelled metric families are registered with bounded label values (metrics_test.go:5-17 label boundedness, :20+ registration; metrics.go:50,54 carry mode/outcome labels).
limitations: Dashboards and CI annotations have no assertions - no dashboard or annotation artifact carries an asserted targeted-vs-full distinction (Prometheus rule files are only syntax-checked per docs/implementation-assessment.md:69) - and CLI report output is untested.

requirements.text: Fast feedback and merge gating are different use cases.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: defaults separate the use cases - FAST_FEEDBACK is the default inner-loop mode with risk-based CI disabled (config_test.go:19-21) and readiness requires a configured full-suite command for authoritative comparison (:22-25).
limitations: The merge-gating half is unasserted: requiresAuthoritativeComparison (run.go:184-189 - OBSERVE always, FAST_FEEDBACK under CI when FinalCIFullSuiteRequired) has no test (internal/cli has only audit_test.go).

requirements.text: Default to targeted inner-loop feedback plus authoritative full CI; risk-based CI gating requires explicit calibration and approval.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: TestDefaultsImplementSafePlannerAndExecutionPolicy (config_test.go:11-26) asserts risk-based CI is disabled by default (:19-21) and TestRiskBasedCINeedsExplicitApprovalAndCompletedCalibration (:181-202) asserts enabling it requires organization owner approval (:198-201).
limitations: Only the owner-approval branch is asserted; the completed-calibration-count branch (server-owned counts, persistence/reads.go:102) is DB-backed and asserted only by CI-only integration tests (quarantine_calibration_integration_test.go:183), and no held-out evaluation of thresholds exists (row IVP-17-8-0044156b18).

requirements.text: Audits are sampled evidence, not a proof of zero misses.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: TestAuditSampleRateIsScopedToPlanMode (audit_test.go:14-37) asserts sampling rates differ by mode (modes.risk_based_ci.audit_sample_rate vs safety.audit.sample_rate) and TestAuditSampleSelectedIsDeterministicAndBounded (:39-57) asserts sample selection is deterministic and bounded - audits are explicitly a sample of runs, never a census (ADR 0004).
limitations: No assertion communicates 'not proof of zero misses' at the report level - audit output shows counts and dispositions but no sampling-coverage statement - and sampling-rate effectiveness is untested.

requirements.text: Always expose denominator, sample size, confidence interval and incomparable runs.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-06: the replay summarizer exposes Wilson 95% bounds (main.go:41-42,199-208) with TestWilsonBoundaries asserting the interval edges (main_test.go:46-53) and counts comparable vs incomparable runs separately (main.go:36,143; main_test.go:21 asserts ComparableRuns=1/IncomparableRuns=1); the production metrics report computes the same Wilson interval over audit totals with comparable/incomparable denominators (reads.go:63-69,162).
limitations: The production report path is DB-backed and has no local assertion (reads.go report query runs only against PostgreSQL, CI-only ci.yml:93) - no test asserts its denominator/CI fields - and sample size is implicit in the comparable-audit denominator and execution count rather than a separately labelled field.

requirements.section_title: Repository layout for the implementation agent
requirements.text: Create this structure from an empty directory.
implementation: Repo tree vs the LLD section 20 outline (docs/Incremental_Verification_Planner_LLD.md:1091-1233): present - go.mod/go.sum/Makefile/LICENSE/Dockerfile/docker-compose.yaml/.env.example/.gitignore/.dockerignore, schemas/ivp-config.schema.json, cmd/{ivp,ivp-api}, internal/{domain,gitutil,config,adapters,analysis,execution,audit,api,persistence,telemetry,security}, config/default-config.yaml, deploy/helm/ivp, tests/, docs/, scripts/

requirements.section_title: Repository layout for the implementation agent
requirements.text: Additional small files are permitted where needed, but responsibilities must remain consistent with these boundaries.
implementation: Actual layout keeps the LLD's responsibility boundaries: one domain package (internal/domain), adapter registry plus per-tool subpackages (internal/adapters), planner (internal/analysis), runner/scheduler (internal/execution), audit classifier/service (internal/audit), router (internal/api), sqlc+migrations (internal/persistence), metrics/tracing (internal/telemetry), redaction/path guards (internal/security)
limitations: The deviations recorded for row IVP-20-8b21868719 (missing .golangci.yml, openapi/, internal/app/, fixtures/examples/testdata, deploy dashboards/alerts, telemetry/logs.go) are permitted as 'additional small files' only by interpretation; no ADR or test records the mapping between the LLD outline and the shipped tree.

requirements.section_title: Repository layout for the implementation agent
requirements.text: The API server and CLI MUST use the same domain/analysis packages.

requirements.section_title: Repository layout for the implementation agent
requirements.text: Do not fork algorithm logic into the CLI.
implementation: grep of CreatePlan( across *.go: definition only at analysis/planner.go:34, production caller only at service/backend.go:375 (plus tests)
internal/cli contains no planner copy - index.go imports analysis for indexing helpers and run.go requests plans from the API

requirements.section_title: Repository layout for the implementation agent
requirements.text: If API connection is unavailable, the CLI may produce only a locally computed full plan unless the policy snapshot is locally signed, unexpired and known compatible with the same algorithm version.
implementation: internal/cli/run.go:316-338 (runOfflineFullSuite: fail-closed authoritative full-suite path when the service is unavailable or untrusted)
internal/cli/run.go:94-105,245-259 (offline detection and dispatch, including stale-worktree refusal)

requirements.text: This section defines dependency order for one implementation pass; it is not a promise to defer capabilities.

evidence: PASS on 2026-11-05: all adapter packages passed - internal/adapters (shared contract tests), generic, bazel, gradle, maven, nx, pytest, jest and builtin - covering discovery, target materialization and result/coverage parsers.

PASS on 2026-11-12: the effective policy carries the bounds (internal/config/precedence.go:180-184) and the whole suite (go test ./... -count=1) is green, so no existing plan changed behaviour - the bounds are far above the fixture graphs.
limitations: The bounds are policy-level constants rather than configuration keys, matching the sibling graph thresholds; an operator cannot tune them without a code change (ADR 0021 decision 4).

A reached bound escalates the whole plan to full verification; the partial traversal result is discarded rather than offered as a degraded selective plan, which is the conservative direction the LLD requires.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Before handing over the repository, the implementation agent must:
limitations: The handover checklist is executed as this inventory review plus the implementation log; each individual item is tracked by its own IVP-APPENDIX-D-* row, and the signed-off DoD checklist is pending (strategy section 5, line 301).

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Run and report every required test command, including the full integration test suite.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: local equivalents of the required commands ran green - gofmt clean, tracker --check, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./... -count=1` (27 packages ok) and `go test -tags e2e ./tests/e2e/ -count=1`; CI runs gofmt, tracker checks, vet, `go test -race ./...` and the e2e gate (ci.yml:29-41) plus the integration job against postgres:16.15 with `go test -tags=integration ./internal/persistence ./internal/service` (ci.yml:71-93).
limitations: The full integration suite (`-tags=integration`, PostgreSQL) and tests/performance are never run locally (BLOCKED, implementation-log.md:42,92) - they run only in CI; the race detector cannot run locally (CGO/GCC unavailable, implementation-log.md:44).

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Provide the actual repository tree and supported adapter versions.
implementation: scripts/generate-repository-tree.py generates docs/repository-tree.md from the repository itself, so the tree and the supported adapter version matrix cannot drift from the code.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: the generator produces the repository tree document (cmd, internal, api and deploy trees plus the adapter version matrix) and the generated document is checked in.
limitations: The adapter version matrix lists the adapter identifiers and their pinned capability strings; the concrete tool versions a user installs are operator choices.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Provide sample successful/failed reports for at least one adapter and document the same contract for all adapters.
implementation: scripts/generate-adapter-samples.py publishes a successful and a failed report for every adapter from the checked-in fixture corpus into docs/adapter-samples/ and its --check mode fails when a sample drifts; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the check.

docs/adapter-samples/README.md documents the shared contract every adapter follows (the success shape, the failure shape, that a setup failure is never a pass, that the classification is identical across adapters and that the samples are sanitized).
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-14: the sample check reports 14 sample reports current (a successful and a failed report for each of the seven adapters), and the shared contract test classifies every fixture of every adapter through one canonical classifier.
limitations: The published samples come from the newest tool version of each adapter; the older versions stay in the fixture corpus and are covered by the contract test.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Demonstrate a confirmed missed-test audit and resulting quarantine in an automated test.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestConfirmedOmittedFailureQuarantines (classifier_test.go:30-39) asserts a confirmed missed test (selected pass vs equivalent full-suite failure) classifies as DispositionConfirmed with Quarantine=true and AuditConfirmedMiss.
limitations: The full demonstrate-audit-then-quarantine scenario (audit_scenarios_integration_test.go, tag integration) requires PostgreSQL and runs only in CI (implementation-log.md:92); locally only the classifier step is asserted.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Demonstrate offline fallback with a stale/expired policy snapshot.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestOfflinePolicyRequiresTrustedUnexpiredCompatibleSnapshot (outbox_test.go:46-66) asserts an untrusted, expired or algorithm-incompatible policy snapshot is rejected by ValidateOfflinePolicy.
limitations: ValidateOfflinePolicy (outbox.go:276-290) has no production caller - offline planning is disabled by design (ADR 0006); the run-side offline full-suite fallback (run.go:316-324) is unasserted, and server.offline_policy is locked to FULL_SUITE_FALLBACK (validate.go:42-44).

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Demonstrate that a passing targeted run is labelled TARGETED_PASS, not FULL_VERIFICATION_PASS.
limitations: Passing selective results are labeled TARGETED_PASS (runner.go:341,401) and the server rejects mislabels - full verification cannot be labeled targeted pass (plans_executions.go:442-455). No test asserts the label end-to-end: execution tests never check the outcome, and the server rejection runs only in the PostgreSQL path (CI-only).

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Demonstrate that a worktree mutation after planning prevents selective execution.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-04: TestRunPlanStopsAfterWorktreeMutation (runner_test.go:112-146) asserts a worktree mutation during execution flips the result to StatusStalePlan/OutcomeStale and stops after the first command, and TestValidatePlanRechecksWorktreePolicyTargetsAndMandatoryChecks (runner_test.go:94-110) asserts ValidatePlan rejects a changed worktree hash before execution.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Provide database migration/restore verification evidence.
implementation: internal/persistence/migrations/001_init.sql ... 007_result_corrections.sql are embedded and applied through goose at API startup (internal/persistence/db.go); the migration bodies that contain dollar-quoted blocks are wrapped in goose statement annotations so they apply as one statement.
internal/persistence/postgres_integration_test.go applies the migrations to an empty database and re-applies them; scripts/verify-postgres-restore-drill.ps1 restores a dump into a fresh database.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-12: the migration suite applies the schema to an empty PostgreSQL (testcontainers) and re-applies it idempotently, and the whole integration suite is green against that schema.
PASS on 2026-11-12: the restore drill script parses cleanly and the database it restores into is exercised by the green integration suites.
limitations: The restore drill against a real PostgreSQL instance is operator-run; the schema application is proven here against a containerized database.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Provide an SBOM, security scan summary, threat-model notes and operational runbook.
implementation: docs/threat-model.md records the assets, the trust boundaries, the threats with the mitigation that implements each of them, and the residual risks.
scripts/verify-required-docs.py asserts that the threat model keeps its assets, trust-boundary, threat and residual-risk sections; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the check.
The SBOM and the vulnerability scan stay in the supply-chain job of .github/workflows/ci.yml, and the operational runbook stays in docs/operations.md.
evidence: PASS on 2026-11-14: the required-document check asserts the threat model's assets, trust boundaries, threats-and-mitigations and residual-risk sections are present, and the supply-chain job still produces the SBOM and the vulnerability scan.
limitations: The model is a design review artifact: it names the mitigation that implements each threat, but the verification of a mitigation stays with the test that owns it.

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: List any unmet SLO or acceptance criterion explicitly.
limitations: Unmet criteria are enumerated in the strategy document's gap registers (sections 3.1/3.2/3.5) and tracked row-by-row in this inventory; the SLO measurement report itself is pending (strategy section 3.5 item 2).

requirements.section_title: Definition of done for the AI implementation agent
requirements.text: Never claim full completion if a required adapter, endpoint, safety rule or test category is missing.
limitations: Completion is never claimed: every row carries an explicit status with code references, the gap registers list open work, and strategy section 5 (line 301) keeps the signed-off DoD checklist pending until acceptance runs are complete.
